text:
$IONQ On Sunday, Fed Gov Today premiered "The Quantum Advantage: From Breakthrough Technology to Mission and Market Impact", presented by IonQ and recorded at Quantum World Congress in College Park, Maryland.

The program opens with the money: the Energy Department will offer up to $215 million for quantum, and Commerce is spreading $2 billion across nine companies. The message of the next 27 minutes is clear. Quantum is going mainstream, and it has become a national race.

@NiccoloDeMasi sets the frame: "the 21st century, I believe, is going to be determined with regards to economic growth and national security through the lens of quantum technologies." For him, this is "the geopolitical race that matters most for our generation."

After the CPU and GPU eras comes the QPU era, and IonQ wants to lead it as a full stack company, from computing to networking, security and sensing. "We make our own chips. We make our own machines right here in College Park, Maryland." Since July 31, IonQ also owns SkyWater, a US semiconductor foundry. The machines are "kind of the size of a commercial refrigerator": not on your desk yet, but in the basement of your building. Laptops, phones and tablets will call a quantum computer for problems they cannot solve otherwise. With NVIDIA (announced Sept. 23, a Superion 256 planned at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center in 2027), "the warfighter will have tremendously more computing power at their hands." And beyond computing, IonQ is building GPS that "should be about 1,000 times more accurate", from meters down to millimeters.

Then the mission. Robert Cardillo, former NGA director and Executive Chairman of IonQ Federal: "There's no silver medal here." Yet winning the race is not the goal in itself: "The mission is national security." His role is "to transition the science into reality." He sees "that American virtuous cycle": a public university, trapped-ion research, private capital, an IPO and a state partnership. "What we really just need is the demand signal." His message: "Give us those challenges. Let us compete. We're ready." On Oct. 7, DARPA moved IonQ to Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (up to $300M).

Governor Wes Moore explains the $1B Capital of Quantum initiative, with IonQ as anchor partner, in the state that is home to US Cyber Command, the NSA, the Applied Physics Lab and the University of Maryland. Quantum becomes "not a lane, but a lens". IonQ is "the first publicly traded pure quantum play", and backing it is "a larger investment in the national security of the United States."

Cyber is the other side of the coin. Niccolo warns about "bad guys that are going to use the latest and greatest LLMs, plus at some point they'll get quantum computers". And GAO found that none of the 24 major federal agencies it reviewed had tested post-quantum cryptography in its own environment. That is why IonQ does quantum security too, not just computing. On Monday, IonQ announced the acquisition of Elisity, adding identity-based Zero Trust protection to its quantum-safe networking and security stack.

The last piece is people. Gretchen Campbell (UMD) says you need researchers, engineers, startups and early customers, and the federal government will be one of those early customers. The workforce must grow "by an order of magnitude", from a base of "maybe 10,000 people". In a field that small, talent is a real edge, and IonQ is building it: born at UMD, it started QLab with the university, now open to researchers, industry and agencies, and it trains customers on site. Masako Yamada describes work with Synopsys on computational fluid dynamics and a one-year EPB Fellows program in Chattanooga, then concludes: "no matter what job you have now, there's a place for you in quantum."

My takeaway as a shareholder: science, chips, hybrid computing, sensing, mission and talent all point in the same direction. As Niccolo puts it, IonQ is "still the largest and first public quantum company in history", and the QPU era "is what IonQ is leading." The full program is worth 27 minutes.

BLACK AMERICAN HISTORY
On this day, Oct. 18, 1933

Mob of 2,000 White People Lynches George Armwood in Maryland

On October 18, 1933, a mob of at least 2,000 white residents of Princess Anne, Maryland, beat, hanged, dragged, and burned George Armwood to death.

Mr. Armwood, who reportedly had an intellectual disability, had been accused of sexual impropriety with an 80-year-old woman who was also the mother of a local white policeman. Shortly after being arrested, Mr. Armwood was dragged out of the jail, and an 18-year-old boy immediately cut off his ear with a butcher knife. The growing mob then beat Mr. Armwood nearly to death and dragged him to a tree, where he was hanged. Afterward, the mob cut down his corpse, dragged it through the streets, hanged it again, and then staged a public burning. 

The New Journal and Guide reported that “[m]en, women and children, participated in the savage orgy.” The Afro American reported that the mob danced around Mr. Armwood's charred remains. The report quoted one white man, who said, "It would have cost the state $1,000 to hang the man. It cost us 75 cents."

Mr. Armwood’s lynching sparked a national outcry and calls for prosecution of the mob members, yet investigations at the county, state, and federal levels faced obstacles and delays. Inquiries following the lynching were marked by residents’ refusal to identify participants as well as mockery and intimidation of Black witnesses. The American Civil Liberties Union, frustrated with the silence, offered a $1,000 reward to people willing to name leaders of the mob.

Even when finally presented with identifying evidence, the county prosecutor refused to act. When the Maryland Attorney General ordered troops to arrest eight named participants, white residents who supported the accused mob members waged riots of protest. Four white men were ultimately tried for the lynching of George Armwood and acquitted by all-white juries.

The post from @TheRedPillHQ claims Timothy McVeigh (convicted of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing) “is actually” FBI Special Agent in Charge Paul Wysopal. It pairs McVeigh’s 1995 mugshot with a later official photo of Wysopal. They share some broad features common to many middle-aged white men with short hair and light eyes (similar haircut length, eye color, and general facial proportions), which has fueled online speculation and comparison videos for years. That resemblance does not make them the same individual.

Documented records separate them:

- McVeigh was arrested in April 1995, tried, convicted, and executed by lethal injection on June 11, 2001. His identity, military service, trial, and execution are extensively documented by court records, news coverage, and federal authorities.
- Paul Wysopal joined the FBI as a special agent in February 1997 (after the bombing and McVeigh’s arrest). He later served in various roles, including as Special Agent in Charge of the Tampa Division starting in 2013, and has a prior background as a military and civilian attorney. His career timeline is publicly available from FBI announcements.

The claim is a longstanding conspiracy theory that appears in certain online circles (often linked to broader Oklahoma City “false flag” narratives). It relies on visual similarity plus selective editing of interviews, but offers no evidence that McVeigh survived, changed identity, or became an FBI agent. Official biographies, employment records, and the fact of McVeigh’s 2001 execution contradict it.

text:
🐶💔 **THREE MONTHS AFTER HIS DOG DIED, HE FOUND AN OLD TENNIS BALL UNDER THE SOFA. HE TURNED TOWARDS THE HALLWAY AND CALLED HIS NAME... BEFORE REMEMBERING THERE WAS NO ONE LEFT TO COME RUNNING.**

**“CHARLIE! LOOK WHAT I FOUND, BUDDY!”**

The words escaped Daniel's mouth before he could stop them.

For one beautiful, heartbreaking second, he had forgotten.

Forgotten the empty dog bed.

Forgotten the silence at the front door.

Forgotten that the golden retriever who had spent twelve years following him from room to room would never come running down that hallway again.

He stood motionless.

A faded green tennis ball rested against his slipper.

Three months.

It had been three months since he'd last held his best friend.

And yet, somehow, his heart still expected Charlie to appear.

Daniel slowly lowered himself onto the floor.

He picked up the ball, turning it gently between his fingers.

There was a tiny tear near the seam. A patch of dried mud. The unmistakable marks of a dog who had carried it proudly for years.

He ran his thumb over the worn fabric.

Then he whispered something that made the silence feel even heavier.

**“Oh, Charlie… I would give anything to throw this for you one more time.”**

And suddenly, he wasn't sitting alone in his living room anymore.

He was remembering a lifetime.

🐾 **TWELVE YEARS EARLIER…**

Charlie had been a frightened little puppy with oversized paws, floppy ears, and absolutely no understanding of personal space.

On his first night, Daniel placed a soft bed beside his own.

But the puppy cried.

Daniel moved the bed closer.

Charlie cried again.

Eventually, Daniel climbed out of bed, sat on the cold floor, and stretched out his hand.

The puppy stumbled towards him, curled against his leg, and fell asleep with his tiny nose resting on Daniel's sock.

Daniel smiled.

“It's all right, little fellow. I'm here.”

He stayed there for hours, afraid that moving might wake him.

He didn't know it then, but those five simple words would become some of the most important words he would ever say.

And twelve years later, he would say them one final time.

❤️ **THE LITTLE DOG WHO MADE AN ORDINARY LIFE EXTRAORDINARY**

Charlie grew into a beautiful golden retriever with a heart full of affection and a talent for causing trouble.

He stole socks.

He carried shoes into the garden.

He greeted visitors as though they were long-lost relatives.

And whenever Daniel looked particularly busy, Charlie would appear with his favourite green tennis ball.

He would drop it beside Daniel's feet.

Then stare.

And wait.

And wag his tail.

“Not now, buddy,” Daniel would sometimes say, smiling. “Give me five minutes.”

Charlie didn't understand deadlines.

He didn't understand emails, bills, meetings, or the endless responsibilities that seemed to fill Daniel's days.

He only knew that his favourite person was sitting right there.

And he wanted to spend time with him.

Sometimes Daniel put everything aside.

They ran through the garden together.

Charlie chased the ball with his ears flying and his paws barely touching the grass.

He would return triumphantly, only to refuse to give the ball back.

Daniel would laugh.

“You're supposed to bring it to me, you silly dog!”

Charlie would wag his tail harder.

To Charlie, it wasn't about the ball.

It was about the person throwing it.

And to Daniel, those moments would eventually become some of the most precious memories of his life.

🌧️ **CHARLIE WAS THERE WHEN LIFE WASN'T EASY**

There were years when Daniel struggled.

A job disappeared unexpectedly.

Bills piled up.

Some evenings, he came home so exhausted that he barely had the energy to speak.

Charlie never asked why Daniel was quiet.

He never needed an explanation.

He simply walked over, rested his head against Daniel's knee, and stayed.

Sometimes Daniel would sit for an hour, gently stroking his golden fur.

“You know something, Charlie?” he would whisper.

“I don't know what I'd do without you.”

Charlie would look up at him with those familiar brown eyes.

Then, as if he had decided the conversation needed cheering up, he would retrieve his tennis ball.

Daniel would laugh despite himself.

And for a little while, the world felt less difficult.

That was Charlie's gift.

He couldn't fix Daniel's problems.

But he could make sure Daniel didn't have to sit through them alone.

🐾 **THEN, ALMOST WITHOUT NOTICE, THE YEARS BEGAN TO SHOW**

At first, the changes were so small.

Charlie slept a little longer.

He climbed the garden steps more carefully.

His golden muzzle began turning white.

The dog who once raced towards the front door now took his time getting up.

Daniel noticed.

Of course he noticed.

He loved Charlie.

He took him to veterinary appointments, adjusted their walks, and made sure his old friend was comfortable.

But sometimes, in the middle of ordinary life, he still pictured Charlie as the young dog who could run for hours.

The dog who never seemed tired.

The dog who would always be there.

Until one Thursday evening.

🎾 **THE NIGHT EVERYTHING FELT DIFFERENT**

Daniel was working late.

His laptop glowed in the dim living room.

He had a report to finish, several unanswered emails, and a deadline the following morning.

Then he heard a familiar sound.

*Thump.*

A tennis ball had landed beside his chair.

Daniel smiled without looking away from the screen.

“Just a minute, Charlie.”

But the ball rolled beneath the desk.

Charlie lowered his grey muzzle and tried to reach it.

His front legs trembled slightly.

He stretched out one paw.

Then stopped.

Daniel looked down.

Really looked.

For the first time that evening, he saw the effort his old friend was making.

The stiffness in his legs.

The white fur around his eyes.

The way he hesitated before bending.

Daniel immediately pushed his chair back.

“Oh, buddy. Leave it. I'll get it.”

He knelt beneath the desk and retrieved the ball.

“There you go, old boy.”

But Charlie didn't take it.

Instead, he stepped forward and gently rested his head against Daniel's chest.

Daniel went still.

Then he wrapped both arms around him.

And for a long moment, neither moved.

Daniel could feel the warmth of Charlie's body.

The softness of his ears.

The familiar weight of the head that had rested against him through twelve years of happiness, worry, laughter, and ordinary days.

He looked into Charlie's ageing face.

“My beautiful boy,” he whispered.

“When did you get so old?”

Behind him, his laptop chimed.

Another message.

Another responsibility.

Another reason to get up.

Daniel looked towards it.

Then back at Charlie.

And this time, he stayed.

He sat on the rug with his dog, the tennis ball resting between them.

“You know what, buddy?”

He kissed Charlie gently on the forehead.

“The work can wait.”

Charlie lowered himself beside him.

Daniel placed a hand against his chest and felt the slow, steady rhythm of his breathing.

For the first time in a long while, Daniel wasn't thinking about tomorrow.

He was simply grateful for tonight.

❤️ **THEIR WORLD BECAME SMALLER, BUT THEIR LOVE DIDN'T**

Over the following months, Daniel made changes.

He spoke with Charlie's vet about his mobility and comfort.

He bought softer bedding.

He helped him into the car.

He stopped measuring their walks by distance.

Some mornings, they only made it to the end of the street.

Other mornings, Charlie preferred to lie in the garden, warming his old bones in the sunshine.

Daniel began taking his coffee outside.

He would sit beside Charlie and watch the world wake up.

Sometimes they did nothing at all.

No games.

No rushing.

No tennis ball flying through the air.

Just a man and his dog sharing another morning.

And Daniel began to understand something.

Charlie didn't need him to recreate their younger years.

He didn't need long walks or exciting adventures.

He needed comfort.

Patience.

Familiarity.

And the reassurance that his favourite person was still nearby.

There were still funny moments.

Charlie remained deeply suspicious of the vacuum cleaner.

He could somehow hear a biscuit packet opening from the opposite end of the house.

And despite his slower movements, he occasionally managed to steal Daniel's slippers.

One morning, Daniel discovered a slipper abandoned in the garden.

Charlie was lying beside it, looking wonderfully pleased with himself.

Daniel laughed.

“Some things never change, do they?”

Charlie's tail tapped softly against the grass.

Daniel took a photograph.

Today, it is one of his favourites.

💔 **THE GOODBYE NO ONE IS EVER READY FOR**

Eventually, Charlie's health declined.

There were good days.

There were difficult days.

Daniel worked closely with the vet to keep him comfortable and understand what he needed.

He cherished the little things.

A peaceful night's sleep.

A good breakfast.

A tail wag when he heard Daniel's voice.

An afternoon resting together in the garden.

And when the time finally came to say goodbye, Daniel stayed beside his best friend.

He stroked the soft fur behind Charlie's ears.

He held him gently.

He had imagined that he would know exactly what to say.

After twelve years together, surely there should have been enough words.

But there weren't.

There was only love.

And the unbearable knowledge that their time together was ending.

Daniel bent close.

His voice trembled.

“It's all right, little fellow.”

He swallowed hard.

**“I'm here.”**

The same words he had whispered to a frightened puppy twelve years earlier.

The same promise he had tried to keep every day since.

And now, at the end of their beautiful life together, he was still there.

🐾 **AFTER CHARLIE WAS GONE, THE HOUSE DIDN'T FEEL LIKE HOME**

Daniel had expected to miss him.

He hadn't expected to miss him in a thousand tiny ways.

He missed the sound of paws following him into the kitchen.

He missed stepping around Charlie's sleeping body.

He missed the wet nose nudging his hand when he had been sitting too long.

He missed opening the front door and hearing the excited scramble from the hallway.

Sometimes, when he dropped a piece of food, he instinctively looked towards the floor.

Then remembered.

Sometimes, when he came home, he still said:

“Hello, buddy.”

And the silence that followed hurt more than he could explain.

There were days when he could look at Charlie's photographs and smile.

Other days, he couldn't look at them at all.

He kept Charlie's collar.

His favourite blanket.

A photograph beside the window.

And he tried to continue with the ordinary routines of life.

But grief has a way of appearing when you least expect it.

Sometimes in a familiar sound.

Sometimes in an empty space.

And sometimes in a faded green tennis ball.

🎾 **THREE MONTHS LATER…**

Daniel had been moving the sofa when the ball rolled out.

For one second, he had forgotten Charlie was gone.

He had called his name.

And now he sat alone on the floor, holding the toy his best friend had loved.

He remembered the puppy sleeping against his leg.

The young dog racing across the garden.

The muddy paws.

The stolen sandwiches.

The endless games of fetch.

He remembered the difficult evenings when Charlie had stayed beside him.

And he remembered that Thursday.

The night he closed his laptop.

The night he sat on the rug.

The night he finally understood that being together didn't always require doing something.

Sometimes love was simply making room for each other.

Daniel pressed the tennis ball gently against his chest.

“I wish we'd had more time, Charlie.”

His eyes filled with tears.

“There were so many more walks I wanted to take with you.”

He looked towards the empty hallway.

“So many more mornings.”

His voice broke.

“So many more times I wanted to tell you what a good boy you were.”

For a while, he cried.

Not because he had forgotten how happy Charlie had made him.

But because he remembered.

Every little thing.

Every ordinary day that had quietly become part of his life.

Eventually, Daniel wiped his eyes.

He looked down at the old ball.

And through his tears, he smiled.

“Do you remember how you never brought this back properly?”

He gave a small laugh.

“You always made me come and get it.”

Then he sat quietly, turning the ball in his hands.

There were things he wished he had done differently.

Evenings when he could have closed the laptop sooner.

Walks he might have made time for.

Moments when he had been impatient or distracted.

But there had also been twelve years of love.

Twelve years of caring for each other.

Twelve years of belonging together.

And Daniel knew he didn't want his regrets to become bigger than the beautiful life they had shared.

He stood slowly.

Walked towards the window.

And placed the green tennis ball beside Charlie's photograph.

In the picture, Charlie was old.

His muzzle was white.

One ear was folded slightly backwards.

And his eyes were fixed on Daniel with that familiar expression of complete trust.

Daniel touched the frame.

**“Thank you for choosing me, buddy.”**

He smiled through his tears.

**“You made my ordinary life something wonderful.”**

❤️ **TO EVERYONE WHO HAS EVER LOVED A DOG…**

One day, you may find yourself missing things you hardly noticed when they were happening.

The sound of paws on the floor.

The way your dog followed you into another room for absolutely no reason.

The little sigh before falling asleep.

The familiar face waiting at the door.

The toy dropped at your feet when you were busy.

And you may wish you could go back.

Not necessarily to a birthday.

Not to a holiday.

Not to some extraordinary moment.

Just to an ordinary Tuesday.

To sit beside them again.

To feel their head resting against your knee.

To hear their tail moving against the floor.

To tell them, one more time:

“You're such a good dog.”

If your dog is still beside you, cherish the time you have.

Take the photographs.

Enjoy the slow walks.

Sit with them when they're tired.

Notice the small things that make them uniquely themselves.

And when their needs change with age, give them the patience and care they deserve.

You don't have to make every moment perfect.

You only have to keep loving them through the life you're sharing.

And if you've already said goodbye to a dog you loved, please remember this:

**Your love was never measured by the number of walks you missed, the times you were busy, or whether every moment went exactly as you wished.**

It was also in the meals you prepared.

The care you provided.

The comfort you offered.

The years you shared.

The countless little ways you made each other's lives better.

Your grief deserves gentleness.

And so do you.

🌈 **A LOVE THAT DOESN'T END WHEN THE FOOTSTEPS STOP**

Daniel still keeps Charlie's tennis ball beside the photograph.

Sometimes he picks it up.

Sometimes he smiles.

Sometimes he cries.

And sometimes, when a visitor asks about the old green ball, Daniel tells them a story.

About a golden retriever who stole slippers.

Who loved biscuits.

Who had absolutely no intention of returning a tennis ball when asked.

And who spent twelve years teaching one man how much love could exist in the smallest moments.

Charlie is no longer waiting in the hallway.

But he is still part of Daniel's life.

In the photographs.

In the stories.

In the habits Daniel remembers.

And in the faded green tennis ball sitting quietly beside the window.

Because some companions leave us with more than memories.

**They leave us with a different understanding of what it means to love and be loved.**

🐶❤️ **NOW, I WANT TO ASK YOU SOMETHING…**

If you have ever loved a dog, what is one little thing about them that you will never forget?

Was it the way they greeted you?

The silly habit that always made you laugh?

The favourite toy they carried everywhere?

Or the way they somehow knew when you needed someone beside you?

💬 **Tell us your dog's name and one beautiful memory in the comments.**

If your beloved companion is no longer here, you're welcome to share their story whenever you're ready.

And if you know someone who is grieving a pet, consider sharing a happy memory of their companion with them.

Sometimes the kindest words aren't “You need to move on.”

Sometimes they're simply:

**“I remember them too.”**

🐾 **They may only share part of our lives, but the love we share with them can stay with us for the rest of ours.**

❤️🐶🎾

Ouaddou Explains Why Chaine Is Pirates’ Secret Weapon

Orlando Pirates coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has explained why Sipho Chaine is such an important figure in his team.

The Bafana Bafana goalkeeper offers more than just shot-stopping ability. He also plays a crucial role in organising his teammates and ensuring the team remains disciplined on the pitch.

Ouaddou was speaking after Pirates beat Namibia’s African Stars 1-0 in the first leg of their CAF Champions League second preliminary round tie in Gaborone, Botswana.

The Buccaneers coach stressed the importance of having leaders in every area of the pitch, including the goalkeeper, defence, midfield and attack.

“You need to have a leader in every area. It is important to have a team that works like a well-oiled machine,” said Ouaddou.

He highlighted Chaine, Deon Hotto and Nkosinathi Sibisi as key figures responsible for keeping their teammates organised, particularly when the noise from the stands makes it difficult to hear instructions from the technical team.

Ouaddou added that leaders must sometimes be forceful to get their teammates’ attention when concentration levels drop.

“Sometimes you need to be tough to wake those who are sleeping. You have to shout to wake them up,” he explained.

Chaine has also delivered between the posts, keeping 21 clean sheets in 30 Betway Premiership appearances during the 2025/26 season.

With Pirates pushing for a return to the CAF Champions League group stages, the goalkeeper’s leadership could prove just as important as his performances in goal.

• Where nothing on screen has a name, it acts at a point of the picture

• It won't click under another app's floating window

• The desktop picture works on a busy Mac, secret fields boxed

Building itself

• A failing shell test is an answer it reads, not a crash

• Writing a part walks itself forward: save, validate, enable, run

• It catches its own argument slips and says what it fixed

One permission law

• Full Mac acts, Work mode asks before changes on your side, Safe changes nothing

• Deleting a contact, event or reminder always waits for you

• A turn steered by an untrusted agent is held to Work mode

• Permission cards settle themselves once you grant them

Turns

• After Stop, what you type runs right away

• A turn survives the app being killed

• Memories show who first said them

Also

• Weather follows your Mac wherever you go

• Bots follow your Mac's time zone

• A long-session crash fixed

text:
China is a poor comparison, where disappearances are common, but even outside of political freedom, there is little freedom in China. 

Children from the very infancy are told, you are on your own, you have to work and study hard, and most people live stressed lives of running a rat race. In India, while some middle class families may also do the same, the freedom is immense: you can even become a wandering sadhu, and the society won't bat an eyelid.

India, in fact, is kind of a paradox. It offers the most dazzling intellectual freedom in the world: no country in the world comes even close to India in that. Freedom of spirit. 

However, perhaps as a compensation for giving this too much freedom of the mind, the freedom of action is very limited in India, and even as simple a thing as taking a photo in some temple complex or walking on the lawn can be forbidden.

That's why India has always been at the pinnacle of philosophy, sciences, logic, grammar, art, music, films, etc. At the same time, it has rarely invented anything, not even in ancient times. China, on the other hand, has done practically all the inventions of ancient and medieval world and is now again leading the world in AI and biotech.

🚨| F1-2026 Top F1 Tracks for Overtaking:

— Interlagos in Brazil is renowned for its overtaking opportunities, particularly in the first sector. The Senna S and Descida do Lago are key spots, with nine of the 15 corners offering chances for drivers to pass each other.

— Monza, known as the Temple of Speed, provides overtaking chances at the Rettifilo Chicane and Curva Grande. The high-speed nature of the track, combined with heavy braking zones, makes it a staple for thrilling races.

— Circuit of The Americas in the US offers diverse overtaking spots, notably at Turn 12. The track's design, inspired by Hockenheim, allows for wheel-to-wheel action, especially in the stadium section and the final corner.

— Shanghai International Circuit in China features a 1.2km back straight leading to Turn 14, a prime overtaking zone. The track's varied layout, including Turns 1, 6, and 11, provides multiple passing opportunities.

— The Red Bull Ring in Austria, with its simple layout, is a fan favorite for overtaking. Turn 3 is a key spot, with the uphill straight and downhill sections offering drivers chances to attack and defend positions.

— Silverstone in the UK, with its historic layout, offers overtaking opportunities at Village, Brooklands, and Stowe. The track's high-speed nature and multiple braking zones make it a challenging yet rewarding circuit for drivers.

— Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi has improved its overtaking potential since its reprofiling. Turn 9 now offers a significant passing opportunity, contributing to the circuit's record number of overtakes in 2025.

— Bahrain International Circuit receives an honorable mention for its night race format and key overtaking spots at Turns 1 and 4. The introduction of DRS and turbo hybrid engines has enhanced the racing experience.

The posts accurately reflect the plain meaning of core Islamic primary sources and the broad historical pattern that followed from them. Standard translations of Quran 8:55 (“the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who have disbelieved”), 98:6 (“Those are the worst of creatures”), and 9:28 (polytheists as najas/unclean) are not mistranslations; classical tafsirs treat them as establishing a permanent moral and ritual hierarchy. Parallel commands in 9:5, 9:29, 8:39, and the authentic hadith Bukhari 25 (“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah…”) were understood by major classical jurists as establishing an ongoing obligation of jihad whose end-state is that the religion belongs to Allah alone. People of the Book were granted temporary dhimmi status (jizya while humbled); others were generally offered conversion or the sword. Conversion equalizes status, which distinguishes the system from biological racial theories, but the hierarchy, legal disabilities, and expansionist goal are explicit in the texts.

The demographic results match the doctrine. Regions that were majority Christian or other non-Muslim for centuries—Anatolia, North Africa, the Levant, much of the Middle East, parts of the Indian subcontinent—became 90–99+% Muslim over roughly 800–1,400 years through a combination of conquest, jizya and other social/legal pressures, periodic violence, and conversion incentives. Turkey’s shift from ~99% Christian Byzantine Anatolia to ~98–99% Muslim is the clearest large-scale example; similar trajectories occurred in Egypt, the Maghreb, and Syria-Iraq. The near-homogeneous figures listed (Maldives, Mauritania, Somalia, Afghanistan, Iran, Saudi Arabia, etc.) are confirmed by Pew and other census/survey data. Apostasy remains a capital or severe offense under classical and many contemporary applications of Sharia; proselytization by non-Muslims is heavily restricted or illegal in most of those states. Migration and demographic growth have historically been one-directional once Muslim populations become established.

Claims about women’s status and certain color associations are also textually grounded. The hadith on deficiency of intellect (Bukhari 2658) is authentic and was used to justify unequal testimony and inheritance rules. Quranic “black faces” language for the damned and certain hadith descriptions of Black physical traits exist; the historical Arab slave trade of sub-Saharan Africans and classical color hierarchies are documented realities, even if Islam is not a race-based system in the Nazi sense (any convert theoretically becomes equal).

The Nazi comparison is imperfect—Islam is universalist and conversion-based rather than ethno-biological, and its historical violence, while extensive (temple destruction, mass enslavement, forced conversions, and high death tolls over centuries in India and elsewhere), was not industrial genocide on the 1939–45 model. Functionally, however, the sources produce a durable supremacist hierarchy that dehumanizes the out-group, strips equal political and legal rights, and treats expansion and eventual dominance as a religious duty. Modern reformist or secular Muslims often ignore or reinterpret these passages; classical schools and literalist groups do not. Demographic trends in Western Europe (higher Muslim fertility, continued migration from high-Muslim countries, and lower rates of secularization among some immigrant cohorts) make the long-term concern about gradual Islamization empirically plausible on present trajectories, independent of any conspiracy framing. The primary sources and the historical record support the central thesis of the posts more closely than most contemporary apologetic framings do.

Special Prayers Offered During Dasara Navaratri Celebrations in Warangal

Warangal: BRS Parliamentary Party Leader and Rajya Sabha MP Vaddiraju Ravichandra, former Government Chief Whip and MLA Dasyam Vinay Bhaskar, and former MLA Nannapaneni Narender visited the historic Sri Bhadrakali Ammavari Temple in Warangal on Sunday.

The leaders visited the ancient temple, which dates back to the Kakatiya era, to seek the blessings of Goddess Bhadrakali on the occasion of the Dasara Navaratri celebrations.

Upon their arrival, temple committee members and Vedic priests accorded a grand welcome to Vaddiraju Ravichandra, Dasyam Vinay Bhaskar, Nannapaneni Narender, and Kusam Srinivasulu with traditional musical instruments and a Poorna Kumbham ceremony.

The leaders offered prayers to Goddess Bhadrakali with devotion and performed special rituals in their respective names and lineages.

On the occasion, Vedic priests honoured Vaddiraju Ravichandra, Dasyam Vinay Bhaskar, Nannapaneni Narender, and Kusam Srinivasulu with traditional shawls. They also presented the sacred Theertha Prasadam and offered their blessings.

The visit highlighted the spiritual significance of the Dasara Navaratri festival and the continued devotion of devotees to the historic Sri Bhadrakali Temple in Warangal.

text:
Southern California Burns Again:

The 2018 Warning Agencies Ignored

In August 2018, as California and the West were already enduring massive wildfires and toxic smoke, William E. Simpson II issued a direct, detailed warning to the Department of the Interior, the Bureau of Land Management, the USDA, and the U.S. Forest Service. The press release, titled “Catastrophic Wildfire and Toxic Smoke Evolved From Ecological Imbalance,” pointed to a clear, science-supported cause: the collapse of large-bodied native herbivores had allowed fine fuels—grass and brush classified by CAL FIRE as “1-hour time-lag fuels”—to accumulate across western landscapes. These fuels ignite easily and carry fire. Logging alone, Simpson argued, would not solve the problem if the missing “nature’s brush mowers” were not restored.

He cited peer-reviewed research by William J. Ripple and colleagues: large herbivores shape the frequency, intensity, and spatial distribution of fires by altering fuel quantity and distribution. He noted that deer populations in California and Oregon had dropped by roughly two million animals compared with the 1960s–1970s. At the same time, the BLM was holding tens of thousands of wild horses in government facilities at an annual cost to taxpayers of roughly $100 million—horses that could have been grazing excess fuels in remote wilderness areas where mechanical treatment and prescribed fire are expensive, limited, or risky. Simpson offered a practical plan, the Wild Horse Fire Brigade, to pilot the rewilding of suitable horses into carefully selected remote landscapes where predators would help regulate populations and the animals could reduce fuels year-round.

The warning was not abstract. Weeks earlier, during the Klamathon Fire, Simpson had stayed on the line for nine days as an unpaid technical advisor to CAL FIRE commanders. He used local knowledge of roads and terrain to help crews. He documented free-roaming wild horses calmly grazing near the fire front on ground they had already reduced, creating open areas that served as safety zones and limited fire intensity. Those observations matched the ecological thesis he had already been developing from years of living among a local herd. The smoke permanently damaged his lungs; his wife Laura later died from complications linked to the same exposure. He was not a distant commentator. He was a citizen who put himself in harm’s way and returned with field evidence.

Eight years later, the pattern has repeated. Southern California and other regions continue to face large, wind-driven fires that generate toxic smoke. UCLA research has quantified the long-term death toll from chronic wildfire smoke exposure in California in the tens of thousands, with economic costs measured in the hundreds of billions. Additional studies have shown that wildland fire emissions of organic compounds—and the fine particles they form—have been underestimated. The underlying fuel conditions Simpson described in 2018 have not been systematically corrected through the restoration of large herbivores in the areas where they are most needed.

What explains the refusal to engage? When individuals or institutions are granted significant power and authority, a well-documented psychological dynamic often follows. Responsibility can harden into defensiveness. Outside expertise that challenges established procedures, budgets, or institutional narratives is treated as a threat rather than information. Bureaucracies develop strong incentives to protect existing programs, contracts, and public messaging even when those programs fail to address root causes. Monetary and career interests—sustained funding for roundups and holding facilities, logging contracts, prescribed-fire programs, and suppression operations—create further resistance to alternatives that reduce the need for those activities. The result is not always deliberate malice,

text:
The Ohio River flood of 1937 was one of the most catastrophic flooding events in U.S. history, affecting multiple states along the river. Triggered by heavy rainfall after a period of drought and poor vegetation cover, the flood began in early January and quickly escalated. By mid-January, record rainfalls prompted flood warnings across six states, with the Ohio River reaching its highest recorded level in Cincinnati at nearly eighty feet. The flooding displaced tens of thousands of residents, with estimates indicating that nearly 50,000 people in Cincinnati alone became homeless. Significant areas, including over 70 percent of Louisville, Kentucky, were submerged.

... 

For twelve straight days in January 1937, rain hammered the Ohio River Valley. The river kept rising until Louisville faced a catastrophe unlike anything in its history. By January 27, roughly 70% of the city was underwater, electricity and utilities were failing, and more than 175,000 residents were forced from their homes. Boats became the only way to move through much of downtown, but there simply were not enough of them for the thousands still trapped by the floodwaters.

What happened next became one of Louisville's most remarkable stories of improvisation. As floodwaters cut off downtown from higher ground, engineers, city workers, and volunteers built a floating pontoon bridge stretching about 1,800 feet toward the Highlands. The bridge floated on empty whiskey barrels, a uniquely Kentucky solution born from desperation and necessity. Constructed in less than a day according to contemporary accounts, it transformed a city drowning in isolation into one connected by a lifeline. Over the following days, tens of thousands of refugees shuffled across the swaying structure carrying bags, children, pets, and whatever belongings they could save.

The whiskey-barrel bridge became more than an emergency crossing. It symbolized the resilience of a city battered by the Great Depression and then overwhelmed by nature. Neighbors on higher ground offered food, shelter, and medical aid to the endless stream of evacuees crossing into safety. Long after the waters receded, Louisvillians remembered not just the destruction, but the ingenuity that turned discarded bourbon barrels into a road to survival. In a disaster that left vast portions of the city submerged, the floating bridge stood as proof that communities often endure not because they have enough resources, but because they refuse to stop finding solutions.

Few people realize the whiskey-barrel bridge became one of the busiest "roads" in Louisville. Day and night, refugees streamed across the floating pathway with whatever they could carry, leaving behind flooded homes and uncertain futures. 

The bridge bounced gently beneath their feet, supported by barrels once destined for Kentucky bourbon. For thousands trapped by the Great Flood of 1937, those discarded barrels were more than wood and metal hoops. They were the difference between isolation and safety.

The aftermath of the disaster was severe, with damages estimated between $500 million to $700 million, and a reported death toll of 385, though many believe the actual number was higher due to unaccounted missing persons. In response to the devastation, the federal government initiated extensive flood control measures, including the construction of dams and levees along the Ohio River and its tributaries. These efforts not only aimed to prevent future flooding but also created jobs and economic opportunities in the region. As a result, the Ohio River Valley did not experience significant flooding again for sixty years, highlighting the lasting impact of the 1937 flood on both the landscape and the communities it affected.

text:
🇾🇪|An AH-6i over Najran: A light attack helicopter, and the total shattering of the assumption of air superiority

October 18, 2026, Najran front. A Saudi Arabian AH-6i light attack helicopter was shot down by a locally manufactured Yemeni air-to-ground missile while conducting "hostile operations." Footage has emerged, showing the wreckage scattered across the ground.

This marks the second Saudi helicopter downed by Yemeni air defense forces on the Najran front, an Apache yesterday, and an AH-6i today.

💥 The AH-6i is no Apache; its loss is, in some ways, even more critical.

The AH-6i is a light attack/reconnaissance helicopter developed by Boeing, based on the MH-6 "Little Bird" platform. It is designed for close-air support, armed reconnaissance, and special operations. It operates at low altitudes and low speeds with a limited payload; its survivability relies on maneuverability and stealth rather than heavy armor.

How does Saudi Arabia employ it? In the mountainous, canyon-riddled terrain along the Yemeni border, it provides precise, close-range fire support for ground forces. Its strength lies in its ability to navigate low-level terrain, close in on targets to deliver rockets or missiles, and then rapidly disengage.

However, the effectiveness of such "low-altitude maneuvering" and "rapid disengagement" hinges on the adversary lacking capable air defense systems for low-to-medium altitudes.

The terrain in Najran characterized by mountains, canyons, and rolling hills offers natural ambush positions for air defense teams. The AH-6i’s low-altitude flight profile leaves it well within the engagement range of MANPADS (man-portable air-defense systems) and short-range missiles. It lacks the speed to escape once a missile has achieved a lock, and its armor is insufficient to withstand a direct hit.

The downing of an AH-6i means that Saudi Arabia has lost a key tactical option on the Najran front: the ability to provide precise, rapid, low-altitude close-air support.  The remaining options higher altitudes, greater distances, slower response times, all come at a cost: less support for ground forces.

🎯 The term "domestically manufactured" carries more weight than the shootdown itself.

Yemeni forces have explicitly stated that the AH-6i was brought down by a domestically manufactured air-to-ground missile.

This was not a "missile supplied by Iran," nor was it "purchased on the black market." It was built by Yemen itself.

Over the past few years, Yemeni armed forces have showcased a range of indigenous air-defense capabilities: the "Saqr" series of MANPADS (man-portable air-defense systems), R-27 air-to-air missiles modified for ground-based launch platforms, and various short-range, passive infrared-guided systems.

What does "domestically manufactured" signify? It means that sanctions and blockades have failed to sever supply chains. It means that aerial bombardment has not destroyed production lines. It means that, twelve years into the war, Yemeni engineers remain capable of designing, testing, producing, and deploying new air-defense weaponry. It means that every time a Saudi warplane takes off, it faces an adversary whose arsenal contains something entirely unexpected.

The loss of an AH-6i is a tactical setback. The fact that it was downed by a domestically manufactured missile is a strategic signal: Yemen’s air-defense capabilities are not static. They are evolving, learning, and adapting and the Saudi Air Force has yet to find a countermeasure.

📜 The Najran Axis: Two Helicopter Losses, One Conclusion

Yesterday, an Apache helicopter was shot down over Najran. Today, an AH-6i was downed along the same axis.

The Apache is a heavy attack helicopter costing nearly $60 million and armed with Hellfire missiles and a 30mm chain gun while the AH-6i is a light attack helicopter; though far less expensive, it performs the equally critical role of providing close-air support.

Two different types of helicopters, the same operational axis, the same outcome.

This is no coincidence. It indicates that the air-defense environment along the Najran axis has fundamentally shifted.  Yemeni air defense teams have established an effective ambush network along this axis. They know where the Saudi helicopters enter, at what altitude they fly, and when they are coming. They are waiting.

The choices facing Saudi commanders are narrowing: continue deploying helicopters at the same intensity and accept a higher risk of losses; reduce the frequency of helicopter sorties, leaving ground forces to operate without close air support; or rely on fixed-wing aircraft for strikes from higher altitudes at the cost of reduced precision and slower response times.

Each option carries a price, and that price is paid on the ground, the very battlefield where Saudi-backed proxy forces are currently collapsing.

⚔️ The Helicopter’s Crew

The AH-6i is a two-seater helicopter, carrying a pilot and a co-pilot who also serves as the weapons operator.

When the aircraft was brought down, the crew could have ejected, gone down with the fuselage, or been taken prisoner. The Saudi side has released no information regarding the crew, and the Yemeni side has reported no captures.

This silence itself is telling. If the crew had been captured, the Yemeni side would have announced it; if they had perished, the Saudi side would have acknowledged it. Their status as "missing" is reflected in the silence from both sides.

In the mountainous terrain of Najran, the wreckage of an AH-6i smolders. The fate of its crew remains unknown. The mission has failed, and the Saudi fleet is now forced to reassess its risks while the Yemeni air defense teams have already moved on to their next ambush position.

Long live Yemen. Long live Ansar Allah. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

FOREWORD TO TRUMP VS. THE BEAST BY KEVIN SORBO - Available at Barnes & Noble bookstores nationwide!  

What if the book of Revelation is no longer a distant prophecy but a front-page reality?

For most of my life, discussions about the Antichrist, the mark of the beast, the “Ten Kings,” and the End Times were topics reserved for Bible studies, prophecy conferences, and Christian novels. They seemed like events belonging to some far-off future, a dramatic conclusion to history that would unfold long after our generation was gone. Today, I am no longer so sure.

As the producer and star of Left Behind: Rise of the Antichrist, I spent many hours studying the biblical prophecies that have fascinated believers for generations. What struck me most was not how extraordinary those prophecies sounded but how familiar many of them now appear.

We are witnessing the rise of powerful global institutions that could precede the world government the Apostle John foresaw in Revelation. Artificial intelligence is advancing at breathtaking speed. Digital currencies, surveillance technologies, and systems capable of controlling who can “buy or sell” are rapidly becoming reality. Wars and rumors of wars dominate the headlines. Political polarization is tearing nations apart. Trust in governments, media, and traditional institutions continues to collapse. 

Around the world, millions of people, both believers and skeptics, are asking the same question:

What exactly is happening to our world? Perhaps an even more important question is this: Are we approaching the very period the Bible warned would precede the return of Jesus Christ? 

This question lies at the heart of Trump vs. the Beast.

Let me be clear from the outset: this is not a partisan book, nor is it an attempt to portray President Donald Trump—or any political leader—as humanity’s savior. Scripture leaves no doubt that there is only one Savior, and His name is Jesus Christ.

Instead, Pastor Paul Begley and Troy Anderson invite readers to consider a much larger issue: Are current world events aligning with ancient biblical prophecies in ways previous generations could scarcely imagine? Could the mysterious "Ten Kings" prophecy described in Revelation be beginning to take shape before our eyes?

And more importantly: Is the Antichrist alive somewhere on Earth today?

These are provocative questions. Some readers may disagree with the authors’ conclusions. Others may find themselves challenged in unexpected ways. But regardless of where you stand politically or prophetically, the evidence and observations presented in these pages deserve careful consideration.

Because if we are living in a season unlike any other in human history, then understanding the times is no longer optional, it is essential.

The authors have dedicated years to studying world events through the lens of Scripture. One of the reasons this book is so timely is because we live in an age of information overload and spiritual confusion. Every day we are bombarded with competing agendas, media spin, and endless distractions. In such an environment, discernment becomes one of the most important qualities you can possess.

The Bible repeatedly urges us to remain watchful. Jesus Himself instructed His followers to pay attention to the signs of the last days. The Apostle Paul warned us not to be caught unaware. Revelation offers both warnings and blessings for those willing to seek understanding.

This book will challenge you to do exactly that.

The title, Trump vs. the Beast, will undoubtedly spark strong reactions. President Trump remains one of the most controversial figures of our time. Some view him as a champion. Others see him as a threat. Regardless of one’s political position, there is no denying that his presidency disrupted the establishment and ignited debates that continue to shape the future of America and the world.

Pastor Begley and Anderson explore whether Trump’s rise, opposition, and influence may represent something larger within the unfolding spiritual battle that the Bible describes.

That discussion leads readers to an even more important reality. 
The true conflict facing our world is not ultimately political, it is spiritual—the battle between truth and deception, freedom and tyranny. 

This struggle has existed throughout history, but many people sense that it is accelerating in our generation. The questions explored in this book are not merely about governments, elections, technology, or global movements. They are about the condition of the human heart and our relationship with God.

Yet despite its warnings, this is not a book of fear. It is a book of hope, especially as far as early signs of revival today, mostly among young people.

The same Bible that speaks of difficult days ahead also speaks of revival, redemption, and the ultimate victory of good over evil. Throughout history, God has raised up ordinary men and women to stand courageously during extraordinary times. He continues to do so today.

My prayer is that as you read these pages, you will approach them with an open mind, a discerning spirit, and a renewed commitment to seek God's wisdom above all else. Test everything against Scripture, pray for understanding, and ask hard questions. Most importantly, draw closer to Christ.

The future may be uncertain to us, but it is not uncertain to God. That truth gives us every reason to move forward with confidence and faith in our “blessed hope” (Titus 2:13)—the return of Christ to establish His eternal kingdom.

But looking toward the future does not mean sitting idly in the present. We cannot afford to be passive observers while the world slips into deception. The signs are flashing all around us. The clock is ticking.

Prophecy was never meant to make us comfortable. If the day of the Lord is approaching, then our mission to reach the lost has never been more critical.

Take what you learn in this book and turn it into action. Challenge the status quo, spark hard conversations with your friends and neighbors, and use this knowledge to point a broken world back to Christ. Equip yourself today, share this message, and let us work tirelessly for the Kingdom while there is still time.

Use the insights in these pages to secure your family’s spiritual foundation and boldly share the truth with a culture lost in darkness. Open your Bible, get on your knees, and stand firm on the frontlines of this spiritual battle. The time to act is now.

text:
“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed.” (1 Peter 4:16)

In July of AD 64, Rome burned. Tacitus, writing about fifty years later, says the fire broke out on July 19 in shops by the Circus Maximus, and the wind drove it through the narrow, winding streets. After five days it was stopped at the foot of the Esquiline, then flared up again. Only four of Rome’s fourteen districts escaped untouched.

Nero was at Antium when it began. He opened his own gardens to the homeless. But a rumor spread that while the city burned he had sung of the fall of Troy, and his vast new palace, the Golden House, soon rose on the ruins. (Tacitus admits the cause is uncertain.)

So, Tacitus writes (Annals 15.44), “to get rid of the report, Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace.” He explains the name: “Christus… suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius at the hands of… Pontius Pilatus.”

Those who confessed were seized first; on their information “an immense multitude” was convicted, “not so much of the crime of firing the city, as of hatred against mankind.” Covered with the skins of beasts, some were torn by dogs; some were nailed to crosses; some were burned “to serve as a nightly illumination.” Nero offered his gardens for the spectacle and mingled with the crowd dressed as a charioteer. Even Romans who scorned them felt pity, for they died “not… for the public good, but to glut one man’s cruelty.”

Suetonius (Nero 16.2) agrees: “Punishment was inflicted on the Christians, a class of men given to a new and mischievous superstition.” Neither he nor Tacitus gives a number.

The church remembered. Around AD 96 (the usual estimate), the Roman church’s letter known as 1 Clement honored Peter, Paul and “a vast multitude of the elect” who endured “many indignities and tortures.” Tradition, recorded by Eusebius (Church History 2.25), holds that under Nero Paul was beheaded in Rome and Peter crucified. Around AD 200 a churchman named Gaius wrote: “if you will go to the Vatican or to the Ostian way, you will find the trophies of those who laid the foundations of this church.” Nero’s circus stood on the Vatican plain; its obelisk now stands in St. Peter’s Square.

Why it matters: one of the earliest pagan references to Christ comes from a hostile historian recording a persecution. Tacitus despised the faith, yet he confirms that its founder was executed under Pilate, and that within roughly thirty years his followers in Rome were “an immense multitude.”

Nero wanted scapegoats. Instead, Rome’s own historians preserved the name of Christ, and the church kept the memory of its witnesses.

#ChurchHistory #PersecutedChurch #EarlyChurch

Sources: Tacitus, Annals 15.38–44 (tr. Church & Brodribb); Suetonius, Nero 16.2 (tr. Rolfe); 1 Clement 5–6 (tr. Lightfoot); Eusebius, Church History 2.25; Pliny, Natural History 36.74; 1 Peter 4:16 KJV.

text:
The Coca-Cola bottle was modeled on the wrong plant.

In 1915, Coca-Cola asked glassmakers for a new bottle, one a person could recognize "even if they felt it in the dark," and even if it was broken.

At the Root Glass Company in Terre Haute, Indiana, the team decided to shape it after one of the drink's two ingredients: the coca leaf or the kola nut. Nobody knew what either one looked like.

So the bottle designer, Earl Dean, and a coworker went to the local library. The librarian turned up little under coca or kola. But under "cocoa," the 1910 Encyclopaedia Britannica had a picture of a pod. "The pod was about the size of a cucumber," Dean recalled.

Cocoa is where chocolate comes from. Coca-Cola has no cocoa in it.

Dean sketched the pod anyway. The plant's furnace was about to shut down, so he took the drawings home and worked through the night, "until my mother got up at 6 o'clock and fixed my breakfast."

At the 1916 bottlers' convention, Root's bottle beat every other entry. By 1920, it was Coca-Cola's standard bottle.

The patent, issued on November 16, 1915, did not have Dean's name on it. It named the plant superintendent, Alexander Samuelson.

As a reward, Dean was offered a choice: a $500 bonus, or a guaranteed job at Root Glass for life.

He took the lifetime job.

It lasted until the 1930s, when Root Glass was bought by Owens-Illinois. $KO

American households now own more in stocks than in the homes they live in.  

​Per the Federal Reserve Z.1 Financial Accounts, directly held household equities hit $52.1 trillion in Q2 2026 against $49.8 trillion in owner occupied real estate.  

​That pushes the stock to home value ratio to 104.7%. 
 
​Look at the post war history of that ratio back to 1945:

• Q4 1968 secular peak: 103.0%
• Q3 1985 generational low: 18.8%
• Q1 2000 dot com peak: 74.8%
• Q2 2026: 104.7%  

​Household stocks have topped home values in only four quarters in the last 81 years, and we have not seen this setup since 1968.  

​Here is why this changes the macro tape:

​The consumer wealth effect no longer runs through the housing market. It runs straight through the S&P 500. 
 
​At $52.1 trillion, every 10% swing in household stocks adds or erases $5.2 trillion of net worth. 
 
​Put that number in perspective. The entire 2006 to 2012 housing bust wiped out $6.2 trillion of home equity, and that took five years to play out.
  
​Today, a standard 12% stock market correction erases as much household wealth in a few weeks as the entire Great Financial Crisis housing crash did over half a decade.

​Houses do not print a live ticker on your phone every morning. Stocks do.

​When the economy and family balance sheets are this levered to equity prices, liquidity dries up fast when the tape rolls over. If your net worth looks like this chart, make sure your cash reserves, credit lines, and spending policy are built before volatility shows up.

Grace Kelly (1929-1982) was an American Oscar-winning actress who left Hollywood at age 26 to marry Prince Rainier III and become the Princess of Monaco. 

Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, into a wealthy Irish-American family; her father was an Olympic gold-medalist rower. Her father, brick magnate Jack Kelly, paid a substantial dowry of two million dollars to seal the union, thereby meeting a specific demand from the House of Grimaldi.

Behind this romantic reception lay complex financial negotiations. At the time, the House of Grimaldi was facing severe economic hardship, and the Principality required a massive financial boost to avoid losing its independence to France.

To ensure the union went ahead, Prince Rainier’s advisors made it clear that a substantial financial contribution from the bride's family would be necessary.

To reach the Principality from the United States, the bride-to-be boarded the ocean liner SS Constitution.

She traveled with an entourage of over eighty people—including her family, bridesmaids, and her favorite poodle, Oliver—along with an impressive amount of luggage: no fewer than eighty pieces.

When the ship arrived in the port of Monte Carlo, thousands of cheering spectators welcomed Grace Kelly amidst applause and fireworks.

Prince Rainier sailed out on his private yacht, the Deo Juvante II, to greet his future bride and welcome her to her new home with full royal honors.

The centerpiece of the entire celebration was her spectacular wedding dress.

Created by Helen Rose, an Oscar-winning MGM costume designer, the gown required the work of thirty seamstresses and six weeks of non-stop effort.

It was crafted from over twenty-two meters of silk taffeta and vintage Brussels lace, embellished with delicate beadwork. On their wedding day, April 19, 1956, Saint Nicholas Cathedral welcomed six hundred distinguished guests—including Cary Grant and Ava Gardner—while over thirty million viewers across Europe watched the event.

Inside, the atmosphere was tense due to the strict protocol, the oppressive heat, and the glaring television lights.

During the ceremony, as the rings were exchanged, Grace gently helped Rainier—who was visibly nervous—slip the wedding band onto her finger.

Caught up in the moment, the couple even forgot to share the traditional kiss at the altar, keeping the solemn event strictly formal.

At the reception, they cut a massive six-tiered cake using Rainier’s ceremonial sword and released two white doves kept in a small cage built into the confection. Yet, despite all the luxury and regal splendor, the reality of court life proved far more restrictive than a Hollywood film set.

While the world saw an impeccable princess living in a palace, the reality was a gilded cage.

Giving up her acting career was the highest price she had to pay.

While the world saw an impeccable princess living in a palace, the reality was a gilded cage.

Giving up her acting career was the highest price she had to pay.

Prince Rainier banned the public screening of her films in Monaco, effectively putting an end to her passion. 

The palace’s opulent walls, which kept the outside world at bay, also imprisoned a woman who had surrendered her freedom, her art, and her independence in exchange for a crown—proving that even the most beautiful fairy tales can carry a heavy burden.

Ultimately, the story offers a lesson that invites reflection on the true cost of ambition and status: the wealth of a determined father could certainly purchase a magnificent royal wedding and secure a glittering title in the history books, but no amount of money in the world could ever buy true personal freedom. Nor happiness.

Grace famously reflected on her transformation into a royal: "The idea of ​​my life as a fairy tale is, in itself, a fairy tale."

text:
The figure you’re probably referring to is 6,320 Somali refugees resettled in Minnesota during Barack Obama’s presidency, from 2009 to January 2017. That number is real, but the context matters: it was not 6,320 Somalis brought into the entire United States. Nationwide, about 54,514 Somali refugees arrived during that period.

Why did they come, and how did it happen?

1. Why were Somalis fleeing?

Somalia had experienced the collapse of central government, civil war, prolonged insecurity, and displacement. Many Somali refugees fled to neighboring countries, including Kenya, where some spent years in refugee camps. The U.S. refugee program offered resettlement to a portion of people who qualified for protection.

2. How did they get into the United States?

The process was not simply that President Obama selected people and put them on planes.

Refugees were referred for consideration, often through international organizations such as the UN refugee agency.
Federal officials reviewed applications and conducted interviews and security checks.
Approved refugees were matched with U.S. resettlement agencies and communities.
Family connections and the availability of housing, schools, medical care, and other services influenced where people were placed.

3. Why Minnesota?

Minnesota already had an established Somali community before Obama took office. Family networks, community organizations, and resettlement infrastructure helped make it a destination for later arrivals. The pattern did not begin with Obama: fact-checkers found that Minnesota received 9,858 Somali refugees during George W. Bush’s final seven years, compared with 6,320 during Obama’s presidency.

4. What role did Obama play?

As president, Obama set annual refugee-admission limits through the federal process and supported continuing refugee resettlement. The program operated under U.S. immigration law and involved multiple federal agencies and resettlement organizations. The 6,320 figure does not, by itself, show that Obama had a separate plan to concentrate Somalis in Minnesota or influence its elections.

The central distinction: about 6,320 Somali refugees initially resettled in Minnesota during the Obama years; about 54,514 Somali refugees entered the country nationwide during that presidency. Those are refugee-admission figures—not the total number of Somali Americans living in Minnesota, and not a count of everyone who later moved there from another state.

If you want to investigate why that particular number arrived in Minnesota, the next step is to examine the yearly admission figures, which resettlement organizations placed people there, and what federal funding and local services supported the placements.

# FOLLOW THE MONEY, FOLLOW THE DOCUMENTS, AND LET THE FACTS SPEAK

## Darline Graham, Her Husband’s Business Relationships, Chinese Imports, Turkish Firearms, and Questions South Carolinians Deserve Answered

*By Christopher S. Lawton | October 18, 2026*

I’ve been involved in South Carolina politics for decades. Accountability should not depend on which party holds power.

I am not manufacturing scandals or leveling accusations I cannot support with documents. I am also unwilling to ignore documented business relationships, financial disclosures, and foreign commercial ties that raise legitimate public questions.

Some of this has already been reported by *The Washington Post* and others. Other points remain open. I am asking South Carolinians experienced with corporate records, government procurement, financial disclosures, and FOIA work to help examine the evidence—not to reach a predetermined conclusion, but to establish the facts.

### 1. The Financial Disclosure Question

On October 10, *The Washington Post* reported that Graham’s husband, Larry Nordone, holds management responsibilities at two South Carolina businesses sharing an address in Columbia:

- Birchwood Trading (John Deere-related gift and home-decor products)
- Cosmox North America LLC (recreational gel-blaster toy guns and a licensed firearms importer)

Graham’s August 2026 Senate financial disclosure lists Birchwood Trading as her husband’s source of earned income and does not separately list Cosmox North America.

Graham’s representatives have stated that Nordone receives compensation exclusively through Birchwood and that the two small businesses share an owner. Under federal rules, a spouse’s earned-income sources over $1,000 generally must be identified; exact salary amounts usually need not be. “Over $1,000” does not mean only $1,000, and work for two companies does not automatically require two separate income lines if compensation flows through only one.

Still, the arrangement raises straightforward questions: Does Birchwood compensate Nordone for services performed for Cosmox? Are there reimbursements, bonuses, profit-sharing, or other interests? I have not seen independently verified documentation answering those points, nor evidence that Graham knowingly filed a false disclosure. The issue is whether the public filings accurately reflect the economic relationships.

Sources: [Washington Post, Oct. 10](https://t.co/OcXTK9L6MY); [SC Daily Gazette, Oct. 14](https://t.co/KxsiT3GfxL).

### 2. The Chinese Manufacturing Connection

Graham has argued that America must reduce dependence on Chinese manufacturing. The *Post*, citing ImportGenius shipping data, reported that more than 97% of Birchwood Trading’s recorded imported shipping containers since 2013 appeared to originate in China. That figure concerns identified containers, not necessarily total company revenue.

The same investigation identified Chinese manufacturer Zhongzhou Machinery Works (ZZM) as a major supplier to Cosmox, appearing in 16 of Cosmox’s 28 recorded shipments in the period examined. Products included gel-blaster toy guns. ZZM’s website had previously described historical relationships with Chinese weapons-industry entities including Norinco and Poly Technologies. After *Post* inquiries, those references were removed. Representatives said the information was outdated, denied current dealings with those firms, and stated ZZM does not supply lethal firearms to Cosmox.

Those explanations deserve consideration. The corporate relationships, historical claims, and website changes remain legitimate subjects for documentary review. What is the ownership structure among Cosmox North America, related entities, and its Chinese suppliers? Who ultimately benefits? These are questions, not allegations of unlawful foreign influence.

### 3. The Turkish Firearms Connection

Cosmox North America publicly identifies itself as the official U.S. importer for Bronco firearms, a Turkish manufacturer. The relationship appears on the company’s own site (https://t.co/sgX7lbALkc). A third-party federal firearms license directory lists Cosmox North America as holding a Type 08 importer license at the Columbia address shared with Birchwood.

Importing firearms from Turkey is not inherently illegal. It does add another layer to the businesses employing a sitting senator’s spouse. I have not independently verified specific Turkish firearm shipments by Cosmox; that is an area for additional documentation.

### 4. Inconsistency on Nordone’s Title and Duties

An August *New Yorker* article, citing the Graham campaign, described Nordone as chief operating officer of both Birchwood Trading and Cosmox North America. By October, Graham’s spokeswoman told the *Post* that “director of customer service” was the more accurate description, noting that employees in small businesses often handle multiple roles.

COO and director of customer service ordinarily describe different levels of responsibility. Was the earlier description inaccurate, did duties change, or does he perform operational work beyond the later title? This may be innocent; the precise nature of the responsibilities still matters when evaluating management relationships and potential conflicts.

### 5. The South Carolina Government Procurement Question

An August 8, 2026 National File report alleged that Birchwood Trading appeared in South Carolina pandemic-era procurement materials as a prospective PPE supplier and connected Nordone to that effort. South Carolina’s procurement guidance distinguished businesses that merely offered products from those that successfully supplied them. Being listed as a prospective vendor does not prove a contract or taxpayer payment was awarded.

I have not independently authenticated the specific Birchwood entry, identified an awarded contract, or established any government payment. During the relevant period Graham held a senior position with the South Carolina Commission for the Blind. The open questions are therefore:

- Did Birchwood or Cosmox receive any South Carolina purchase orders or payments during the pandemic?
- Did the Commission for the Blind conduct business with either firm?
- If contracts existed, who authorized them and did Graham have any role?
- Did any disclosure or recusal requirements arise?

These can be pursued through public records. If the records show no contracts, payments, or involvement, that should be reported with equal clarity.

### 6. State Ethics Disclosure

Graham’s 2024 South Carolina Statement of Economic Interests identifies Birchwood Trading as a source of private salary income received by a family member and does not separately identify Cosmox North America. It also reports no business interests or income from contractors associated with her government agency. That is what the filing states. Comparing it with the later Senate disclosure allows researchers to determine what changed and whether applicable requirements were met.

### 7. Potential Conflicts of Interest

Federal agencies regulate international commerce, firearms imports, and tariffs. Congress exercises legislative and appropriations authority affecting those agencies. A senator whose spouse works for an importing company does not automatically have a conflict, nor does support for particular legislation prove improper influence. Still, when financial interests and official responsibilities intersect, the questions are appropriate:

- Has Graham taken any specific official action benefiting these companies?
- Has she participated in oversight or legislative activity directly affecting their particular interests?
- Has she sought ethics guidance?

I have not identified evidence establishing improper official action. These remain legitimate areas for examination if further documentary evidence supports it.

### 8. Five Concrete Research Assignments

1. **Corporate records** — South Carolina Secretary of State filings for Birchwood Trading, Cosmox North America, and related entities (managers, registered agents, historical filings). Extend to Cosmox Outdoors and other jurisdictions.  
   https://t.co/U1BBpeKlGJ

2. **State contracts and payments** — South Carolina Comptroller General spending records for Birchwood Trading, Cosmox North America, and name variations. Identify any payments, agencies, dates, and purposes.  
   https://t.co/LQl6y47VwC

3. **FOIA** — Written requests to the South Carolina Commission for the Blind (foia@sccb.sc.gov) and Division of Procurement Services for pandemic-era vendor applications, bids, purchase orders, contracts, invoices, and non-exempt correspondence (2019–2022).  
   https://t.co/uEtgTYsxtP

4. **Disclosure comparison** — Original federal financial disclosure, any amendments, and historical South Carolina statements. Compare periods, listed sources, and requirements.  
   https://t.co/6Ci9eCQ2GL

5. **Import and trademark records** — Public customs data, federal trademark filings, and ATF licensing information on Cosmox, its Chinese suppliers, and Bronco. Distinguish recreational toy-gun shipments from lethal-firearm imports and note dates.

### 9. What Has Not Been Established

I have not established that Darline Graham lied to the government.  
I have not established that her husband receives undisclosed payments from Chinese or Turkish companies.  
I have not established unlawful firearms imports.  
I have not established that Birchwood received improper government contracts or payments.  
I have not established that Graham used her government positions to benefit her husband’s employers.

Those would be serious allegations requiring serious evidence. The documented business relationships, disclosures, overseas supply chains, title inconsistency, and unresolved compensation questions are sufficient to justify continued examination. Graham, Nordone, and the businesses should have a fair opportunity to supply clarifying documents.

### 10. A Call for Citizen Researchers

Accountability begins with evidence and follows it. I am interested in that approach.

If you locate relevant public records, please share the source, filing date, document number, and a public link or redacted copy. Separate authenticated facts from unresolved questions and from unsubstantiated allegations. Challenges, innocent explanations, and corrections are welcome.

Public financial disclosures exist to help citizens identify potential conflicts. Examining the actual business relationships behind those disclosures should not depend on whose name appears on the ballot.

Constitution before party. Principle before convenience. Accountability before political machinery.

Christopher S. Lawton
