17 1 That great whore is described, 2 with whom the Kings of the earth committed fornication. 6 She is drunken with the blood of Saints. 7 The mystery of the woman, and the beast that carried her, expounded. 11 Their destruction. 14 The Lamb’s victory.

1 Then [a]there came one of the seven Angels, which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come: I will show [b]thee the [c]damnation of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters,

2 With whom have committed fornication the kings of the earth, and the inhabitants of the earth are drunken with the wine of her fornication.

3 [d]So he carried me away into the wilderness in the Spirit, and I saw a woman sit upon a [e]scarlet colored beast, full of names of blasphemy, which had seven heads, and ten horns.

4 And [f]the woman was arrayed [g]in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, [h]and had a cup of gold in her hand full of abomination, and filthiness of her fornication.

5 [i]And in her forehead was a name written, A mystery, [j]that great Babylon that mother of whoredoms, and abominations of the earth.

6 [k]And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of Saints, and with the blood of the Martyrs of JESUS: and when I saw her, [l]I wondered with great marvel.

7 [m]Then the Angel said unto me, Wherefore marvelest thou? I will show thee the mystery of that woman, and of that beast that beareth her, which hath seven heads and ten horns.

8 [n]The beast that thou hast seen, [o]was and is not, and [p]shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and shall go into perdition, and they that dwell on the earth, shall wonder (whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world) [q]when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.

9 [r]Here is the mind that hath wisdom, The [s]seven heads [t]are seven mountains, whereon the woman sitteth: [u]they are also seven Kings.

10 [v]Five are fallen, [w]and one is, [x]and another is not yet come: and when he cometh, he must continue a short space.

11 [y]And the beast that was, and is not, is even [z]the eighth, and is [aa]one of the seven, and [ab]all go into destruction.

12 [ac]And the ten horns which thou sawest, are [ad]ten kings, which yet have not received a kingdom, but shall receive power, as Kings [ae]at one hour with the beast.

13 [af]These have one mind, and shall give their power and authority unto the beast.

14 These shall fight with the [ag]Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of Lords, and King of Kings: and they that are on his side, called, and chosen, and faithful.

15 [ah]And he said unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, [ai]are people, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.

16 And the ten [aj]horns which thou sawest upon the beast, are they that shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate, and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.

17 [ak]For God hath put in their hearts to fulfill his will, and to do with one consent for to give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God be fulfilled.

18 And that woman which thou sawest, is that [al]great city which reigned over the kings of the earth.

Revelation 17:1 The state of the Church militant being declared, now followeth the state of the Church overcoming and getting victory, as I showed before in the beginning of chapter 10. The state is set forth in 4 chapters. As in the place beforegoing I noted, that in that history the order of time was not always exactly observed, so the same is to be understood in this history, that it is distinguished according to the persons of which it treateth, and that in the several stories of the persons is severly observed in the time thereof. For first is delivered the story of Babylon destroyed, in this and the next chap. (for this Babylon out of all doubt shall perish before the 2 beasts and the Dragon). Secondly is delivered the destruction of both the two beasts, chap. 19. And lastly of the Dragon, chap. 20, in the story of the spiritual Babylon are distinctly set forth the state thereof in this chap. and the overthrow done from God, chap. 18. In this verse and that which followeth is a transition or passage unto the first argument, consisting of a particular calling of the Prophet (as often heretofore) and a general proposition.
Revelation 17:1 That is the damnable harlot, by a figure of speech called hypallage. For S. John as yet had not seen her. Although another interpretation may be borne, yet I like this better.
Revelation 17:1 The sentence that is pronounced against this harlot.
Revelation 17:3 Henceforth is propounded the type of Babylon, and the state thereof in 4 verses. After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.

Early life
Sako was born in the city of Zakho, Iraq, on 4 July 1948.[3] He comes from an ethnic Assyrian family of the Chaldean Catholic Church that has roots in a religious community that has had a presence in the city of his birth since the 5th century AD.[4]

He was ordained a priest on 1 June 1974 and filled his first pastoral assignment at the Cathedral of Mosul until 1979. He then earned a doctorate in Eastern patrology at the Pontifical Oriental Institute. Revelation 17:1 The state of the Church militant being declared, now followeth the state of the Church overcoming and getting victory, as I showed before in the beginning of chapter 10. The state is set forth in 4 chapters. As in the place beforegoing I noted, that in that history the order of time was not always exactly observed, so the same is to be understood in this history, that it is distinguished according to the persons of which it treateth, and that in the several stories of the persons is severly observed in the time thereof. For first is delivered the story of Babylon destroyed, in this and the next chap. (for this Babylon out of all doubt shall perish before the 2 beasts and the Dragon). Secondly is delivered the destruction of both the two beasts, chap. 19. And lastly of the Dragon, chap. 20, in the story of the spiritual Babylon are distinctly set forth the state thereof in this chap. and the overthrow done from God, chap. 18. In this verse and that which followeth is a transition or passage unto the first argument, consisting of a particular calling of the Prophet (as often heretofore) and a general proposition.
Revelation 17:1 That is the damnable harlot, by a figure of speech called hypallage. For S. John as yet had not seen her. Although another interpretation may be borne, yet I like this better.
Revelation 17:1 The sentence that is pronounced against this harlot.
Revelation 17:3 Henceforth is propounded the type of Babylon, and the state thereof in 4 verses. After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.

Conditional Realism: Mutual Recognition Before Automatic Sympathy

My stance on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is neither one of adherence to any government nor of automatic political sympathy. It is a conditional realism: I demand mutual recognition as a prerequisite for granting collective legitimacy, I distinguish between individuals and projects, and I consider a distant horizon only as a remote possibility.

The core lies in the historical record. The organized Palestinian leadership has rejected concrete paths toward a Palestinian state: the 1947 partition plan, the Camp David offer in 2000 (a state in most of the West Bank and Gaza, territorial adjustments, and a presence in Arab Jerusalem, without a formal counterproposal), the Clinton parameters, and the Olmert proposal. As long as there is no leadership that credibly accepts the permanent existence of Israel, I do not support the current Palestinian cause, nor UNRWA in its present form, nor the BDS movement.

This does not deny individual suffering, nor is it opposed to those within Palestinian society who want coexistence and are fed up with the war. I recognize and, where appropriate, defend these people—Muslim, Christian, atheist, or agnostic. What I reject is the framework that treats Israel's existence as the problem to be solved and uses refugee status as a permanent tool.

I can criticize Netanyahu, settlement expansion, radical settlers, or IDF excesses without that obligating me to legitimize the other side. The practical difference between living in Tel Aviv or Ramallah remains observable in terms of rights and freedoms; therefore, if I had to choose, I would prefer Israeli symbols, although ideally I would avoid both.

Regarding solutions, the classic partition is blocked, a unitary state is unfeasible due to demographics and security, and total annexation will not happen. A binational confederation with a shared capital in Jerusalem seems to me, in the abstract, the least bad arrangement if the conditions ever arose. But I don't present it as the realistic path, nor as the only correct one: it's a highly improbable horizon and a last resort. The same actor that failed to reach disengagement agreements would have to accept a much more demanding framework in terms of trust and shared sovereignty. 

Until I see that change in leadership, I won't promote it. My operational position is clear: I don't support the current Palestinian cause, and I prioritize the framework that, in practice, allows for greater functionality.

This stance may be called “Zionist or pro-Israel” by those who demand automatic sympathy for the Palestinian side. I experience it as selective humanism and conditional realism: respect for those who seek peace, a demand for mutual recognition, and a refusal to use suffering as an argument to keep open a conflict that has had opportunities to be resolved.

"Zelensky could have stopped the war" - how, exactly? Look at what was actually on the table.

What Ukraine offered: Kyiv has repeatedly proposed freezing the war along the current front line. That means de facto accepting Russian control of the occupied territory for now. Zelensky said so publicly again in June 2026. He also offered a full ceasefire for the duration of talks and a face-to-face meeting with Putin. Putin dismissed the meeting as pointless and said the army should "do the job."

What Russia demanded: Russia wants Ukraine to withdraw from the part of Donbas it still holds and hand it over without a fight. That area is Ukraine's main fortified defensive belt, the line that has stopped Russian offensives for years. Giving it up would leave the road to central Ukraine open the next time Russia attacks. At times Moscow has demanded all four regions it "annexed," including areas it never captured. Russia also rejects any Western troops in Ukraine as a security guarantee, so Ukraine would be asked to give up its defenses and get no guarantee that Russia won't come back.

Where it stands now (October 2026): According to Reuters, Putin will only return to negotiations after Ukraine gives up the rest of Donbas. In other words, he wants the concession before talks even start. The 2022 Istanbul talks broke down over similar issues: Russia wanted caps on Ukraine's army and a veto over any security guarantees.
So the choice was never "peace or war." It was "keep fighting, or give up your best defensive line with no guarantee the war won't restart." No country would take that deal.

As for "he got wealthy off it": that's a claim, so show the evidence. Meanwhile, look at what he actually did. When Russian columns were heading for Kyiv in February 2022 and the US offered to evacuate him, he stayed. He knew Russian hit squads had been sent to kill him and his family. A man who wanted to profit from war would have taken the ride and watched from a villa abroad. He has spent four years burying his own people. Saying he wants this war is obscene.

On Starlink: it's not free charity from Musk. Most of the regular Starlink terminals in Ukraine, roughly 29,000, were supplied by Poland, which also pays for the subscriptions. Germany funded around 10,000 more in 2023. Starshield, the encrypted military version that is harder to jam, runs on Pentagon contracts. Starlink isn't responsible for the war, but it isn't a gift either. Governments pay for it.

DAW Books, which published the Gor series from the 8th volume (Hunters of Gor) to the 25th volume (Magicians of Gor), subsequently decided to cease publication of the books, citing low sales;[8]

According to Betsy Wollheim, who took over DAW Books from her father Donald A. Wollheim in 1985,

I alone killed the Gor books. I am personally responsible for rejecting John Norman. ... I am very proud of that. We needed him in the beginning because he sold so well. And in the beginning he didn't write quite as much about female slavery. He was more Burroughs-like. But he got worse and worse and worse and it got to the point where it was demeaning our company to publish them. ... But when I rejected John Norman, he wrote a twenty-page letter to the head of Waldenbooks accusing me of censorship, which was pretty hilarious. The head of New American Library came up to me and said "Why aren't you publishing him?" I said, "Hey, he's yours. Go. Do it. You want to publish him, publish him." If you accuse a publisher of censorship every time they reject a manuscript, then by that definition every manuscript submitted would have to be published. Books would be terrible. A publisher has to have some sort of editorial discretion.[9]

Norman attributed the decision to feminist influences, saying in 1996:

Tarnsman of Gor was published in late 1966. It has been reprinted 22 times... I have recently signed contracts for fresh French and German sales, and have recently been published for the first time in Czechoslovakia. There have been recent Spanish and Italian sales. There's no evidence that my books no longer sell... After DAW refused to buy any more Gor books, I sold a three-part Telnarian series to Brian Thomsen of Warner Books. The first book, The Chieftain, had a 67 percent sell-through. The second, The Captain, had a 91 percent sell-through, which is the sort of thing that would make Stephen King rush over to shake your hand... Brian Thomsen, my Warner editor for the Telnarian series... was replaced by an editor from one of the blacklisting presses, one that explicitly informed my agent they would not consider anything by John Norman. That new editor canceled the series despite its success and without waiting to see how the third book, The King, would do. That way things are made nicely clear...

Unfortunately for me, only about seven or eight publishing houses maintain a mass-market paperback line in science fiction and fantasy; this small, closely-knit group effectively controls the market. With such a group, a blacklist need not be an explicit, formal written or oral agreement subscribed to by a gathered cabal pledged to secrecy. It is an understanding that a certain individual is to be ostracized, excluded, methodologically overlooked or such.[10]

Starting in 2001, John Norman's books were published by E-Reads as ebooks and print copies. According to their website, "they are among E-Reads' biggest sellers".[11] Open Road Integrated Media acquired E-Reads in 2014.[12]

A notable tactic of abusers is that they will paint their victims in a false light, and do so loudly, yet strategically. They will point the finger and project many of their own behaviors onto the victim, so that people will see them differently and not believe the victim if they ever have the courage to come forward about the abuse they are experiencing.

The abuser will attack their victim’s character, accuse them of substance issues, promiscuity, call them crazy, and do anything they can to discredit them. They will even claim that their victim is abusive. In doing this, the abuser maintains the power and control of how people perceive the situation and the victim.

This makes it much easier to continue the abuse without question. At this point, anything the victim says will be chalked up to mental health issues or be considered invalid. Then the abuse will heighten, and the victim becomes less inclined to speak up because any attempts to do so are met with negative consequence. Not only from the abuser, but from others that have been manipulated to also be silent partners in the abuse.

An abuser is a master manipulator that is very good at twisting the narrative to paint themselves as a victim, and it’s easy for others to fall into the trap if they lack adequate training of these patterns.

Abusers will often utilize systems such as the justice system, law enforcement, medical providers, and other entities, such as the victim’s family, community and religious organization to target the victim as well, isolating them from any type of support or help.

There is a considerable lack of training in fields that are utilized as avenues to empower abuse.

The next time someone boldly speaks negatively about another, it’s wise to sit back and question why they would do so. Speaking ill of another person should be a red flag. There is no other motive of speaking negatively about another person, other than to do them harm. It certainly doesn’t promote anything good, wholesome or helpful.

There are many resources to learn skills to identify these patterns. It’s very possible that a loved one at some point may need your help in identifying these tactics. Everyone should become educated to avoid becoming inadvertent abusers themselves by falling into the trap.
This is a community, family, and overall public responsibility of helpful and contributing citizens.

The VCR 8×8 Dragón is one of the most important and debated programmes undertaken by the Spanish Army in recent decades.

This analysis approaches the project from a technical, operational and industrial perspective, with the aim of separating perceptions, criticism and controversy from the available facts.

The text reviews the programme’s background, the delays accumulated and the different actors responsible for them, as well as the real scope of a family of vehicles intended to replace already obsolete platforms and to redefine part of wheeled mechanised manoeuvre.

Drawing on comparisons with other 8×8 infantry fighting vehicles in service in neighbouring countries, it examines dimensions, weight, mobility, powerpack, protection, armament, vetronics and price.

The result offers a nuanced assessment of the system, its strengths and its limitations, and places the VCR 8×8 Dragón in the context of the present and future needs of the Spanish Land Force.

An editorial entitled ‘Zelensky Is Open to a Starlink Deal’ has been published in WSJ Opinion. And I completely disagree with the main message of this piece.

The WSJ is proposing a deal to Ukraine: we would halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure for 100 days, and in return the US would extend Starlink coverage approximately 300 kilometres into Russia, so that the Ukrainian army could strike missile launchers and drones.

According to the WSJ, this proposal was conveyed to Zelenskyy by Republican Senators Roger Wicker and Kevin Cramer.

The editorial states:

“Ukraine would take a breather from striking Russian energy assets. In exchange the U.S. would expand Ukraine’s Starlink satellite coverage up to roughly 300 kilometers into Russia.”

And further:

“The trade by our lights is worth it.”

In my opinion, no. This is not how relations between allies should look.

Such a deal might at least resemble a fair one if Ukraine were given the full capacity to operate up to 470 kilometres deep into Russia, rather than just 300.

Kharkiv is situated approximately 30 kilometres from the Russian border, Sumy approximately 25–30 kilometres, and Kyiv just over 200 kilometres. Meanwhile, Russia can launch missiles from territory situated considerably further than the proposed 300-kilometre zone.

Therefore, 300 kilometres does not represent parity. It is yet another artificial restriction on Ukraine’s capabilities. A range of up to 470 kilometres would at least have allowed for a significant expansion of the zone within which Russian launchers could not operate with impunity.

First, Starlink and Starshield – which are critically important to the Ukrainian army – are restricted without warning. Such decisions cost Ukrainian lives. Then Ukraine is offered the chance to restore or expand these capabilities in exchange for refraining from strikes on one of the most vulnerable points of the Russian military economy.

This is not a deal. It is blackmail.

At the same time, the WSJ itself acknowledges the obvious:

“Ukraine has every right to raise the pressure on Mr. Putin to stop his conquest.”

This raises a simple question: if Ukraine has this right, why should it have to pay the price of refraining from effective strikes in exchange for the ability to defend itself against Russian missiles?

“But the ability to hit the Russian archer instead of letting the arrows fall is even better.”

But the mere ability to strike at the “archer” must not come at the cost of security guarantees for Russian oil refineries.

Ukraine needs both the ability to destroy Russian launchers and the ability to strike at the infrastructure that sustains the Russian war machine.

For some reason, Russia isn’t making a choice. Why should Ukraine have to choose?

Especially after Trump had already announced some sort of ‘energy truce’ – one that Ukraine and Russia had not, in fact, agreed upon between themselves – whilst Russia continued its strikes.

“A frustrated Mr. Zelensky now says Ukraine will resume targeting Russian energy sites after Mr. Putin ignored Mr. Trump’s announcement last weekend of a “cease-fire” and continued to bomb Ukraine’s energy sites.”

Russia is violating the ‘ceasefire’. Russia continues to strike. Yet once again, Ukraine is being asked to make concessions.

No.

America has been and remains our ally. The American people, Congress, the military and millions of Americans have helped Ukraine throughout the war. That is precisely why, as a matter of principle, I do not wish to equate the United States with the current administration.

Through its recent actions, the current US administration is behaving not as an ally of Ukraine, but as an ally of Russia.

We hope that the American political system will be able to restore relations between the US and Ukraine to a normal alliance model.

Because the normal model is very simple.

Russia is the aggressor.

Ukraine is defending itself.

An ally helps Ukraine defeat the aggressor, rather than haggling with it over the right to defend itself.

DAW Books, which published the Gor series from the 8th volume (Hunters of Gor) to the 25th volume (Magicians of Gor), subsequently decided to cease publication of the books, citing low sales;[8]

According to Betsy Wollheim, who took over DAW Books from her father Donald A. Wollheim in 1985,

I alone killed the Gor books. I am personally responsible for rejecting John Norman. ... I am very proud of that. We needed him in the beginning because he sold so well. And in the beginning he didn't write quite as much about female slavery. He was more Burroughs-like. But he got worse and worse and worse and it got to the point where it was demeaning our company to publish them. ... But when I rejected John Norman, he wrote a twenty-page letter to the head of Waldenbooks accusing me of censorship, which was pretty hilarious. The head of New American Library came up to me and said "Why aren't you publishing him?" I said, "Hey, he's yours. Go. Do it. You want to publish him, publish him." If you accuse a publisher of censorship every time they reject a manuscript, then by that definition every manuscript submitted would have to be published. Books would be terrible. A publisher has to have some sort of editorial discretion.[9]

Norman attributed the decision to feminist influences, saying in 1996:

Tarnsman of Gor was published in late 1966. It has been reprinted 22 times... I have recently signed contracts for fresh French and German sales, and have recently been published for the first time in Czechoslovakia. There have been recent Spanish and Italian sales. There's no evidence that my books no longer sell... After DAW refused to buy any more Gor books, I sold a three-part Telnarian series to Brian Thomsen of Warner Books. The first book, The Chieftain, had a 67 percent sell-through. The second, The Captain, had a 91 percent sell-through, which is the sort of thing that would make Stephen King rush over to shake your hand... Brian Thomsen, my Warner editor for the Telnarian series... was replaced by an editor from one of the blacklisting presses, one that explicitly informed my agent they would not consider anything by John Norman. That new editor canceled the series despite its success and without waiting to see how the third book, The King, would do. That way things are made nicely clear...

Unfortunately for me, only about seven or eight publishing houses maintain a mass-market paperback line in science fiction and fantasy; this small, closely-knit group effectively controls the market. With such a group, a blacklist need not be an explicit, formal written or oral agreement subscribed to by a gathered cabal pledged to secrecy. It is an understanding that a certain individual is to be ostracized, excluded, methodologically overlooked or such.[10]

Starting in 2001, John Norman's books were published by E-Reads as ebooks and print copies. According to their website, "they are among E-Reads' biggest sellers".[11] Open Road Integrated Media acquired E-Reads in 2014.[12]

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is reportedly outselling GTA 6 by nearly 6-to-1 in Amazon U.S. physical preorders right now.

Around 60,000 for Zelda versus roughly 11,000 for GTA 6 over the same recent period.

GTA 6 will be enormous.

But never underestimate the power of hearing those first few notes from an ocarina and suddenly being a kid again.

Some games sell on hype.

Others have had a place in your heart for nearly 30 years.

**No clear evidence of a formal partnership or alliance between Ron DeSantis and the Bush family (or “Bush deep state”) to primary Trump.** The claim is a common rhetorical/conspiratorial framing from parts of the MAGA base during the 2023–2024 primary, not a documented political arrangement.

### What the record actually shows

- **Jeb Bush’s public praise**: Former Florida Gov. Jeb Bush spoke positively about DeSantis multiple times. He attended DeSantis’s 2023 inauguration (reportedly the only former governor to do so), called himself a “Ron DeSantis fan,” praised his effectiveness as governor (including on Hurricane Ian), and said 2024 offered DeSantis an opportunity to run and lead a “generational change” / make Florida a model for the country. Bush later clarified he was “praising, not endorsing.” Trump supporters widely treated the comments as establishment backing.
- **DeSantis’s earlier comments**: In 2018, DeSantis publicly praised George H.W. Bush as an “American hero” who “amassed prodigious accomplishments” and called him “the greatest Yalie of them all” (both are Yale alumni).
- **Shared Florida context**: Both served as Florida governors. DeSantis’s rise built on the state’s Republican shift that began under Jeb Bush and continued under Rick Scott. Some commentary noted policy or stylistic overlaps with pre-Trump Republicans, but this is interpretive.

### What is missing

- No evidence of joint campaign strategy, shared key advisors from Bush circles, major Bush-family donations, or coordinated efforts specifically aimed at taking out Trump. DeSantis’s 2024 inner circle and campaign staff consisted mainly of Florida operatives, some with prior Trump-administration ties (e.g., Dustin Carmack), and standard GOP consultants—not Bush loyalists.
- Donor records show only small contributions from private individuals who happen to have the last name Bush; nothing linking to the political Bush family at scale.
- Contemporary reporting (including from outlets covering the “deep state plant” attacks) described the accusations as conspiracy-style claims circulating among Trump loyalists, often pointing to Jeb’s inauguration attendance or general establishment interest in a Trump alternative. DeSantis himself later used anti-“deep state” language on the campaign trail.

DeSantis entered the 2024 race after Trump had already endorsed him for governor in 2018, underperformed, suspended his campaign after Iowa, and endorsed Trump. He later indicated to donors he would help fundraise for Trump. The “partnered with the Bush deep state” phrasing is political rhetoric rather than a substantiated partnership.

text:
OCTOBER 18, 2026

USA POLITICS WATCH ALERT

VOTER ROLLS: STATES MUST UPHOLD ELECTION INTEGRITY

SUMMARY

An October 9 federal court ruling rejected the Department of Justice's nationwide voter-data collection policy.

Meanwhile, the DOJ has challenged California over more than 20,000 registrations flagged as potentially involving noncitizens.

The central issue is not whether citizenship eligibility should be verified. It is how federal and state authorities can enforce election laws while respecting constitutional limits.

1. WHAT DID THE COURT RULE?

In Common Cause v. Department of Justice, Judge Sparkle L. Sooknanan ruled that the DOJ exceeded its statutory authority and violated federal administrative and privacy requirements.

The ruling invalidated the particular federal data-collection policy, not the government's authority to enforce election laws.

2. STATES HAVE RESPONSIBILITIES

Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections.

States administer voter registration and must maintain accurate voter rolls under applicable federal law.

Reasonable, lawful federal requests for information relevant to voter eligibility deserve substantive cooperation.

States should explain what records they can provide, identify legitimate privacy restrictions and offer lawful alternatives when requests exceed federal authority.

Rejecting one unlawful data-collection method does not eliminate the responsibility to investigate credible eligibility concerns.

3. THE CALIFORNIA DISPUTE

On October 15, the DOJ announced litigation involving more than 20,000 California registrations flagged as potentially belonging to noncitizens.

California disputes the federal allegations.

These records warrant careful examination, but a database flag alone does not establish unlawful registration or voting.

Verification must account for naturalization, outdated records and possible identification errors.

4. THE CONSTITUTIONAL STANDARD

Article I, Section 4 gives states primary responsibility for administering congressional elections while permitting congressional regulation.

Federal agencies must act within the authority Congress grants them. States must comply with applicable federal election requirements.

Neither level of government should use jurisdictional disputes to avoid its legal responsibilities.

5. THE QUESTION FOR THE STATES

What procedures are in place to identify ineligible registrations?

How are citizenship records verified?

How quickly are credible discrepancies investigated?

And how are eligible American citizens protected against wrongful removal?

Election integrity requires more than political assurances. It requires documented procedures, lawful cooperation and measurable accountability.

Noncitizens must not vote in federal elections. Eligible American citizens must not lose their voting rights through inaccurate records.

Both obligations deserve serious enforcement.

SOURCES

U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, Common Cause v. Department of Justice, October 9, 2026.

U.S. Department of Justice, California voter-list litigation announcement, October 15, 2026.

U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 4.

National Voter Registration Act of 1993.

USA POLITICS WATCH
Independent political reporting for the U.S. Republic.

text:
The Seventh Bowl: “It Is Done”
A Dirt Road Devotional

Key Scripture (Revelation 16:17)
“And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done.”

There comes a time when God's patience gives way to His judgment. The seventh bowl reminds us that although God is longsuffering, He will not tolerate rebellion forever. The world has been warned, judgments have fallen, and yet mankind continues to blaspheme the very God who holds its destiny in His hands.

Three words ring out from heaven: “It is done.”

Those words declare the completion of God's appointed judgments. No government can overrule Him, no army can defeat Him, and no earthly power can delay His purposes. When God declares that the time has come, the matter is settled.

Here is the sobering truth: even in the face of devastating judgment, people refuse to repent. Revelation 16:21 tells us that men blasphemed God because of the plague of hail. Their suffering did not soften their hearts; their hearts remained hardened in rebellion.

We ought to take that lesson seriously. It is possible to experience hardship, witness the consequences of sin, and still refuse to turn toward God. Trouble alone does not produce repentance. A heart must be willing to acknowledge its sin and bow before the Lord.

Friend, don't mistake God's patience for approval. Just because judgment has not fallen does not mean judgment will never come. The same God who offers mercy to the repentant is also the righteous Judge who will one day settle every account.

You don't have to wait for the thunder to roll or the ground to shake before you get right with God. Today is the day to heed His Word, confess your sin, and trust Jesus Christ.

Dirt Road Truth: God's patience gives us time to repent, not permission to rebel.

Closing Thought: The most dangerous heart is not necessarily the one that has never heard God's warnings, but the one that has heard them repeatedly and still refuses to listen.

Katie Zacharia started as White House press secretary on a Monday, gave her first briefing Tuesday — 14 minutes long, three questions — and was already 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘶𝘵 of the job by Friday.

The trouble traces back to how she got the job. Trump introduced her as “an attorney” in his social media post naming her press secretary. Mike, I agree that things have to change. That’s why I’ve been vocal about new ideas to support regional breeding. The premise has always been to help programs outside Kentucky, but the real question is whether those regions are willing to help each other and work together. That’s the core of what I’ve suggested.
I’ve long thought concepts like revenue sharing (as we see in other sports) could protect the industry from the bottom up rather than relying only on top-down measures. On the idea of discounts or incentives for state-bred progeny of Kentucky-sired horses, many farms are already doing versions of this and working out deals to help regional breeders get to the next sale. Stallion farms still have bills to pay; they’re not banks. As I said in my note below, I believe breeders' awards should be paid when a foal is born, not when that horse gets to the races. That’s too far down the line, I think. Giving people an incentive on a shorter timeframe is important.
Creating five or six conferences across the country could make stallions more valuable within each region, generate more demand and energy, and help bring people back into breeding. If discounts are going to be offered, I’ve always felt they should prioritize the people willing to breed to race. That approach could reward those people willing to take the higher risk over two to three years and give commercial breeders a bit more space because it’s very crowded right now.
These kinds of practical, cooperative steps seem worth exploring together. Happy to discuss further.

Tarnsman of Gor was published in late 1966. It has been reprinted 22 times... Canada’s historic trade pivot exposes the cost of America’s tariff driven isolationism and the rising strength of India under PM Modi’s leadership.

For decades, Canada sent the bulk of its exports (historically around three quarters) to the United States. 

Recent data show that share has dropped to roughly 67–68% its lowest non pandemic level in decades as US tariffs and policy uncertainty under the current administration force Ottawa to seek alternatives.

Canada’s official response is clear: double non US exports over the next decade, including more than doubling two way trade with India from $30.4 billion (2025) to $70 billion by 2030.

That is why Ottawa just dispatched its largest trade delegation to India in over 30 years nearly 300 business leaders and is racing to conclude a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of 2026.

This is not charity or optics.

The mission has already produced dozens of commercial agreements worth hundreds of millions of dollars in aerospace, clean technology, agri-food, and other sectors.

It builds on a $2.6 billion long term uranium supply deal between Cameco and India, which supports India’s nuclear expansion while giving Canada a strategic energy market.

India offers a vast, growing consumer base, manufacturing capacity, and demand for energy, critical minerals, technology, and resources that a protectionist Washington can no longer reliably provide to its own allies.

The United States has long taken Canadian dependence for granted.

Tariff threats and unilateral pressure have instead accelerated the very diversification Ottawa now pursues. Meanwhile, India’s economy under the Modi led NDA government has delivered consistent growth, infrastructure expansion, and an open, results oriented approach to partnerships making it the partner of choice for countries seeking stability and scale rather than unpredictable confrontation.

Canada is choosing reliability and mutual gain over continued over reliance on a single market that weaponizes trade.

The $70 billion target is ambitious, but the direction is unmistakable: reliable partners are moving toward India because it delivers growth and partnership, while America’s current approach is pushing even its closest allies to look elsewhere.

This is a win for Canada’s diversification, a win for India’s strategic rise under decisive leadership, and a clear signal that protectionism has costs.

text:
Some are saying that because MIT and Whitehead were not held liable, they are exonerated from this mess. Nothing could be further from the truth.

These institutions have sophisticated, eight-figure legal operations and substantial resources devoted to shielding them from liability. They know how to word damaging public statements while protecting themselves against defamation claims. They also know how to invoke attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, and other privileges to shield their dirty business from public scrutiny. Their ability to defend themselves legally should not be confused with institutional integrity.

Faculty employment is generally at will. That means an employer can fire someone for any or no reason. Tenure is a policy, not a legal right. Faculty are sold the promise of its security, but finding out what protections they can actually enforce when push comes to shove can take years and enormous legal fees. Sally Kornbluth, now MIT’s president, even admitted in court once that tenure does not carry the legal protections faculty believe it does (Shaughnessy v. Duke, see her deposition excerpts in the summary judgment materials). Employment law provides no remedy for many destructive decisions universities make.

Civil rights laws offer protection against discrimination, and pursuing those claims is often the only recourse faculty have in court against a university. But proving discrimination is difficult, especially for a scientist with a unique position and record. David pointed to Knouse as someone treated differently. She also ran a laboratory and had NIH funding, but I think the court ruled they were not similarly situated. He did have a more senior rank and a larger lab. So be it.

But discrimination law only addresses discrimination. You can treat people like garbage and run your institution into the ground without committing actionable discrimination. This is where public accountability must come into play.

The jury found that Knouse defamed David and unlawfully interfered with his livelihood. MIT, Whitehead, and HHMI held the authority, and through their actions, the false allegations against him became career-destroying consequences. That is why this verdict demands accountability from those institutions. They bear responsibility for the damage those actions caused.

We speak to the founder and Executive Director of @Genspect Dr Stella O'Malley about the best available evidence for the care of children with gender dysphoria and gender-questioning youth. Dr O'Malley is a prominent international voice in the struggle for the rights of concerned parents and detransitioners. She has been on a speaking tour of Australia and NZ.  

Dr Stella O'Malley's qualifications include a B.A. in Counselling and Psychotherapy, an M.A. in Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, diplomas in Youth Studies, Psychometric Testing, and Gender Identity Counselling and a PhD in Social Work, with research focused on parents’ perceptions of gender dysphoria in children and adolescents. Stella co-authored "When Kids Say They're Trans" (2023) with fellow therapists Sasha Ayad and Lisa Marchiano, to offer a resource for parents who want their children to flourish, but do not believe that hasty medicalisation is the best way to ensure long-term health and well-being. Stella is the founder and Executive Director of Genspect, an international organisation that advocates for a healthy approach to sex and gender. text:
Minnesota Wild vs Columbus Blue Jackets — rested hosts against a side on its second night

Preview · NHL · Regular season · Sunday 18 October 2026

Minnesota finished ahead of Columbus last season, have made the better start to this one and are 3-0-0 in their own building. Columbus arrive on the second night of a back-to-back, a day after a 1-0 overtime win over the Rangers, while the Wild have not played since Thursday. That is enough to pick Minnesota, at medium confidence.

THE MATCHUP

The Wild finished 2025-26 on 104 points at 46-24-12, third in the Central, and beat Dallas 4-2 in the first round before Colorado knocked them out 4-1. Columbus ended on 92 points at 40-30-12, fifth in the Metropolitan, and missed the playoffs.

Kirill Kaprizov scored 45 goals and 89 points last season and has opened this one with nine goals and 14 points in eight games. Quinn Hughes has 12 points and Matt Boldy, a 42-goal scorer last season, has seven.

For Columbus, Zach Werenski had 81 points last season and Kirill Marchenko 27 goals. This season Charlie Coyle leads the team with six points, all assists, and Kent Johnson has four goals.

FORM & CONTEXT

Minnesota are 5-2-1, with 26 goals for and 20 against, 3-0-0 at home and 2-2-1 on the road. The home wins came against Boston (4-1), Vegas (4-2) and St. Louis (5-4 on Thursday), and they lost 2-5 in Winnipeg on Tuesday. Jesper Wallstedt has a .921 save percentage over seven starts.

Columbus are 3-3-0, with 17 goals for and 21 against. They are 3-2-0 at home and 0-1-0 on the road, that game a 3-5 loss in St. Louis. They were beaten 3-7 at home by Florida on Tuesday before edging the Rangers on Saturday. Jet Greaves is at .905 over four starts and Cam Talbot at .822 over two.

The end of last season pointed the same way: Minnesota went 6-4-0 in their last ten, Columbus 2-7-1. Pre-season was the exception: Columbus beat Detroit twice and Pittsburgh, while Minnesota's only win was 3-2 in overtime against Chicago.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

Freshness and home ice. Columbus are 0-1-0 on the road this season and played on Saturday night; Minnesota are rested and unbeaten at home. With Kaprizov in this kind of form, the Wild carry the sharper attack and the steadier goaltending.

The head-to-head offers no lean. Columbus won 7-4 in Minnesota on 11 October 2025, and the Wild won 5-2 in Columbus on 18 December.

THE CALL

Last season's standing, this season's start and the rest advantage all point to Minnesota. The level series and Columbus's pre-season are why it stops at medium.

Minnesota Wild to win, medium confidence.

Process-focused view: Emphasizes what happens when a user engages or pushes. The system can be moved toward stronger evidence; the default is a starting point, not a fixed endpoint.
Capability-focused view: Judges the model by what it is able to produce under scrutiny rather than by the path-of-least-resistance output most people see.

Your outcome-focused standard is legitimate and practical: if the majority of users absorb a left-leaning baseline without effort, that effect is what matters for real-world influence. text:
Will Meta’s Muse Be Mark Zuckerberg’s First Organic Hit Since Facebook, or Just More AI Slop?

@finkd built @facebook more than 20 years ago, then acquired @instagram and @WhatsApp. Despite the tech giant’s resources, few homegrown products have ever created new consumer behaviors at scale. Probably Zero after Facebook. 

Could @Muse finally be his first big organic innovation? I think Muse has a shot, see the attached use retention chart. 

This weekend, I joined a discussion with some top AI investors, researchers, and product experts about personal AI personal assistants.

One person envisioned AI agents applying for lots of jobs while employer’s agents screen résumés, conduct interviews, and reject candidates.

AI generates. AI processes. AI summarizes. Are we just creating more AI slop for other AI to process?

Really? If that’s all we get, I will be very SAD. 

@peterthiel famously said, “We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters.”

That was for mobile cloud era and we finally got the flying cars in 2026 by @elonmusk. 

I hope agentic AI era aims higher too: discovering drugs, extending healthy lives, powering robots, transforming education, and giving us more time to enjoy life.

Watching the next generation build robots (photo) reminds me of the innovation I’d love AI to accelerate.

Let’s measure AI by how much it improves human lives, not how many tasks it completes.

Here are my top 10 items I noted from the AI discussion since many of you are curious:

1. Still reactive. One estimate suggests only 10% of Muse tasks are initiated autonomously.
2. Rapid adoption. First day retention better than ChatGPT (see attached image). Some expects 3M+ DAUs.
3. Boring wins for now. Scheduling, reminders, and tedious chores deliver immediate value.
4. Solo founders love it. Agents boost individual productivity.
5. Memory is the moat. Models are replaceable. Personal context isn’t.
6. Execution beats intelligence. Verified outcomes matter more than clever responses. One personal agent may coordinate many specialists.
7. Access is the battleground. Amazon restricts Muse. Alibaba, Tencent, and J.P. Morgan operate closed ecosystems.
8. Apple is the wildcard. OS control offers an advantage potentially but some researchers do not see Apple has much advantage just because it owns the device and OS.
9. Costs are significant. Estimated at $1 plus per active user everyday. It is a long game but it might benefit the big tech.
10. Monetization remains unproven. Who pays, how much, and for what? Will there ever be a subscription?

One final question from me:

What’s the single biggest bottleneck preventing personal assistants  from making a much bigger impact? Trust? Capabilities? Use Cases?

text:
Anthropic just committed 5% of its shares to a fund for the public good. At the last reported valuation of $965B that is about $48B, and the stake grows every time the company's value jumps 50%.

What Anthropic said today, verbatim: "Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline."

The fund is a wholly owned LLC, not a 501(c)(3). Anthropic's reason: "to give adjustability between different forms of giving." One hard line: "None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad."

Where the "20%" headline comes from: the 5% is new. The rest is old. Co-founders "pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings" at founding, and "approximately half" of employees are in an equity donation match. Add it up and "roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good." The new money is 5%, not 20%.

The line that matters for workers: Anthropic names "labor market impacts" as a target, says AI "could also cause instability for many workers," that "bolder approaches may be needed," and floats "direct distributions to specific populations." That is a frontier lab writing a possible cash-transfer program into its own cap table.

What nobody has yet: the baseline valuation, the governance, who decides what gets funded. Anthropic says those come "in the coming months." Stockholders still have to vote. Until then this is a pledge, not a check.

What it means for your money: nothing lands in anyone's account this year. The signal is the ratchet. Anthropic says it is common for tech companies to offer "escalating compensation awards to their executives" and that it is "instead directing that equity to the public benefit." Every 50% jump adds 2% of a bigger company.

3 things to watch:
1. The baseline. If it is today's $965B, the next 2% needs about $1.45T. If it is an older round, the ratchet may already have tripped once.
2. The governance doc. "Wholly owned" means Anthropic's board controls the fund. Who can say no to the board is the whole question.
3. The stockholder vote. Investors who just paid $965B are being asked to approve handing 5% to an entity the board controls. Watch whether anyone objects in public.

🏢 ENTERPRISE-GRADE DISTRIBUTED DATA SHARING: REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS OF BITTORRENT TECHNOLOGY

While BitTorrent is widely celebrated among consumer audiences, its underlying technology offers massive strategic advantages for enterprise-level operations, big data management, and digital content delivery networks (CDNs). Companies handling large-scale data transfers, such as software updates, video streaming, and game distribution, face huge operational costs when relying solely on traditional cloud server farms.

BitTorrent’s distributed P2P protocol completely transforms enterprise content distribution by offloading bandwidth demands from central origin servers to receiving clients. Tech giants and open-source software foundations regularly deploy BitTorrent protocols to deliver large software builds, operating system images, and heavy data packages globally at a fraction of standard bandwidth costs, with complete uptime reliability.

In the Web3 era, enterprise adoption of BitTorrent technology has further accelerated through BTFS and cross-chain integrations. Media companies, gaming studios, and decentralized AI projects utilize BTFS to store petabytes of user data, game assets, and machine learning models securely on a distributed network. This structure prevents expensive cloud lock-ins, lowers storage overhead, and guarantees uninterrupted data availability.

As global data generation continues to explode exponentially, enterprise demand for scalable, distributed content delivery models will only grow. BitTorrent's proven track record of handling massive data throughput positions it as an essential technology partner for modern digital enterprises.
