text:
🇸🇴❤️ DISCOVER SOMALIA: A LAND OF BEAUTIFUL TRADITIONS, DELICIOUS FOOD AND WARM HOSPITALITY! 🇸🇴

When I watch this video, I feel proud of the richness of Somali culture and the beauty of our traditions. I see more than food, colourful decorations and cultural celebrations. I see a Somalia that welcomes people, celebrates its heritage and has so much to share with the world.

🍽️ I want the world to discover Somali cuisine. Our food is an important part of our identity, bringing families, friends and communities together. From fragrant rice and traditional dishes to freshly prepared local delicacies, Somali cuisine reflects our history, creativity and love of sharing. For me, food is not simply something we eat; it is a way of expressing generosity, friendship and belonging.

🫶 I am proud of our tradition of hospitality. In Somali culture, welcoming guests and sharing what we have are deeply valued traditions. I want visitors to experience that warmth for themselves, to sit with us, taste our food, learn about our customs and leave with wonderful memories of the people they meet.

🎨 I love seeing our culture celebrated. Our traditional clothing, decorations, music, poetry and food tell the story of a proud people with a rich cultural identity. These traditions connect generations and help preserve our heritage while introducing it to younger Somalis and people from other parts of the world.

🌍 I want more people to look at Somalia with curiosity, openness and hope. Too often, Somalia is discussed only in connection with conflict and hardship. Those challenges are real, but they do not tell the whole story. Our culture, our communities, our entrepreneurs, our creativity and our hospitality deserve to be seen and celebrated too.

🇸🇴 I believe Somalia has so much to offer the world. Cultural tourism, Somali restaurants, local food businesses, traditional crafts and community festivals could all help introduce more people to our heritage and create opportunities for Somali people. With continued improvements in security, infrastructure and visitor services, I hope more people will have the opportunity to experience Somalia's culture firsthand.

I would love to see visitors from Africa, Europe, the Middle East and beyond discovering our food, learning our traditions and experiencing the generosity that Somali people are proud of.

I know Somalia still faces challenges, and I do not pretend that everything is perfect. But I believe we can help change perceptions by sharing the positive stories, welcoming visitors, supporting local businesses and showing the world the many wonderful things our country has to offer.

I want people to see Somalia not simply as a country with a difficult past, but as a country with a beautiful culture, proud traditions, welcoming people and a future full of possibilities.

If you have never tried Somali food or experienced Somali hospitality, I hope one day you will get the opportunity. Come with an open mind, discover our traditions and experience our culture for yourself.

May Allah bless Somalia and its people, preserve our beautiful heritage and bring our country lasting peace, stability and prosperity.

Alhamdulillah. I am proud of Somalia, proud of our culture and proud of the hospitality we can share with the world. 🇸🇴❤️

LET'S TALK FOOTBALL WITHOUT BIAS.

I think we're doing Caicedo a disservice with the way we compare him to Declan Rice.

Caicedo is an elite ball-winner, reads danger exceptionally well, dominates duels and protects his defence. Add his press resistance and ability to progress play from deep, and you have a midfielder who does far more than break up attacks.

Rice offers more attacking threat, carries and creativity. Both are exceptional, but they're different profiles. Judging Caicedo by Rice's attacking output misses the entire point.

Last season, Caicedo's defensive numbers in tackles, interceptions and duels won per 90 minutes highlighted his superiority in those areas, while Rice offered more in chance creation.

If I have my way, I'd play both of them on the same team.

text:
Batman movies have made more than $5 billion. For 76 years, every Batman story carried one name: Bob Kane. The man who named Bruce Wayne got a page rate.

The clip below was filmed in the summer of 1989. A caption calls Kane the creator of Batman, and he jokes that one day he will look down from the Batcave in the sky and ask Warner Bros. to send him the residuals.

Kane's first Batman, drawn in 1939, had red tights and stiff bat wings. His writer, Bill Finger, gave him the cowl, the cape, the dark costume and the name Bruce Wayne. Kane got the royalties and the byline. Finger got paid by the page.

In 1965, Kane called the idea that Finger co-created Batman entirely untrue. Years later, in a private interview with his own co-author, he put Finger's share of the creative work at 50 to 75 percent.

Finger died in 1974, at 59. His son scattered his ashes on an Oregon beach in the shape of a bat.

In 2015, after a push by Finger's granddaughter, DC changed the credit line.

"Batman created by Bob Kane."
"Batman created by Bob Kane with Bill Finger."

It took 76 years to add three words. Finger lived to see none of them.

If you had built half of Batman, would you have fought your partner for your name, or waited for him to offer it?

text:
The Nasdaq fell 2.1% on Friday. What stands out more is how broadly tech stocks sold off: just 7 of the S&P 500’s 75 technology constituents finished higher. $AMD fell 6%, $AVGO dropped 4.5%, $MU slid 5.6%, and $INTC lost 5.8%. $META and $GOOGL also ended lower.
This looks less like a problem with any one company and more like the market reassessing the return potential of tech and AI investments.
Until recently, investors expected AI capex to drive revenue growth across chips, networking, memory, and cloud services. Now they’re asking whether that revenue can cover the costs of compute, financing, and depreciation.
A drop in share prices doesn’t mean AI demand has disappeared. But “spending is still increasing” is no longer enough to support a bullish case. $TSM’s strong results show that demand remains resilient, but they don’t, on their own, prove that cloud providers are earning adequate returns, customers are willing to pay for AI services, or financing conditions for capital-intensive projects are sound.
This week’s earnings will offer fresh evidence: $NFLX reports Tuesday, followed by $META, $TSLA, and $LRCX on Wednesday. Orders for chipmaking equipment, ad monetization, and whether deliveries translate into profits and cash flow matter more than simply repeating that “AI demand is strong.”
If orders hold up and revenue and margins keep pace, Friday’s selloff may prove to be a valuation reset. If capex keeps accelerating while earnings lag, pressure on tech stocks could continue.
A pullback alone isn’t a reason to buy, and a few days of losses aren’t enough to declare the AI thesis over. For now, I’m waiting for companies to show with their results that investment is turning into revenue and cash flow.

text:
ARSENAL GOT THE 3 POINTS, BUT THIS PERFORMANCE SHOULD BE A WAKE-UP CALL. 

Arsenal grind out a 1–0 win at the City Ground, making it just our second victory in the last six visits to Nottingham Forest.

Let’s be honest: the first half was nowhere near good enough. We lacked creativity, struggled to break Forest down and offered very little going forward. It’s now three consecutive games where we’ve struggled to create enough in the opening 45 minutes.

The second half was better, though. We played with more purpose, found more openings and our substitutes once again made the difference. Noni Madueke took his goal brilliantly, and it’s great to see him stepping up when the team needs him.

I won’t blame individual players because football is a team sport. But Arteta must find a way to get more out of the players who struggle to influence games when they start. We cannot keep relying on substitutions to rescue our performances.

The biggest concern? Bayern Munich are next midweek. We will need to be at our absolute best against them. The slow starts, lack of creativity and inconsistency in our attacking play must improve because Bayern will punish those weaknesses.

Was this convincing? Absolutely not. Was it an important three points? Without a doubt.

Sometimes you don’t have to play well to win. Today, we found a way, and I’ll take the points.

But against Bayern, we need much more than this.

Three points secured. Improvements needed. COYG!

𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗸𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗸: 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗗𝗔𝗽𝗽 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗡𝗲𝗲𝗱𝘀 𝗠𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗦𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘀

Smart contracts can execute automatically when their conditions are satisfied.

But there is a practical limitation: a contract does not independently wake up, monitor every external event, and initiate transactions whenever something changes.

Automation requires a mechanism to trigger execution, and many use cases also require reliable external data.

That is an important infrastructure challenge for Web3 developers.

WINkLink offers oracle services designed to connect external information with smart contracts, alongside automation capabilities for supported use cases.

Imagine a decentralized application that needs to respond when a predefined condition is met.

The workflow may require an external event to be detected, the relevant information to be delivered on-chain, and the contract to execute according to its rules.

For a DeFi application, this might involve a price-related condition.

For another application, it could involve a scheduled action or a particular external data event.

The important distinction is that automation does not remove the need for good design.

Developers must define the triggering conditions, permissions, failure handling, and safeguards against unwanted execution.

An automated contract can execute flawed logic just as efficiently as correct logic.

That is why the combination of dependable data and carefully defined execution rules matters.

Oracle infrastructure helps applications access the information they need, while automation mechanisms can help reduce the need for manual intervention in supported workflows.

Together, these capabilities expand what developers can build beyond simple transactions that require users to initiate every action themselves.

For the TRON ecosystem, this represents an important area of infrastructure development.

More useful automation begins with reliable inputs, clear rules, and secure execution.

text:
"The Ghost of Empire and the Face of Fascism" 

✍️ Farhana Zinat Barsha (17/10/2026)

When we talk about fascism in Bangladesh, we make a mistake if we think it started in our lifetime.

What we saw; the disappearances, the elections without voters, the police firing on students, the way an entire state was turned into the property of one family and one party; that did not come out of nowhere. It was the afterlife of empire.

The British did not just colonise our land. They colonised our idea of power. For two hundred years they taught us that power is not accountable. That the ruler does not need to listen. That law is a weapon for the ruler, not a shield for the ruled. That dissent is treason. That a Bengali life is cheaper than order. They left in 1947, but the structure stayed. The same Secretariat, the same sedition law, the same police who were taught to see the public as subjects to be controlled, not citizens to be served. We changed the flag, but we kept the machinery. And every authoritarian after that learned how to use that machinery better than the last.

French colonisation taught the same lesson in a different language. It preached liberty at home and practiced empire in Algiers, in Dakar, in Haiti, in the Caribbean. It extracted wealth, then it extracted people, then it told the descendants of those people that they should be grateful to be allowed to live in the margins. Modern fascism is just empire coming home.

In Bangladesh, it came home as a party that started believing it is the liberation war. That no one else can be patriotic. That questioning them is betrayal of the nation. In other parts of the world, it comes home as parties who say the nation is being "invaded" by immigrants, by Muslims, by students, by anyone who reminds them that empire had a cost.

The script is identical:
1. Invent an enemy.
2. Convince people they are in danger.
3. Offer yourself as the only savior.
4. Then make the exception permanent — emergency laws, special powers, no accountability.

That is how you go from colonial subject to fascist citizen without ever noticing the shift. This is also why I see the same struggle everywhere today. Whether it is students in Dhaka in July, or people protesting in France right now against police violence and the rise of the far-right, they are all refusing the same colonial logic; control the narrative, criminalise the street, protect the institution, not the people. We got political independence, but we never got freedom from the idea that power can be absolute, unquestioned, and inherited.

That's why I say; 'No one can make you free unless you fight and achieve it yourself. (Pretty Witch Quotes, 10/09/2017)"

Freedom was never gifted. Not in 1947, not in 1971, not in July 2024. Freedom is not charity. It is not given by any empire, any party, or any savior-leader who says "I am the state."

Fascism wants us to feel isolated. Colonialism wanted us to feel inferior. The antidote to both is to fight and achieve it ourselves not to replace one untouchable leader with another, but to replace the whole idea that any leader should be untouchable. And this is where we have to stop lying to ourselves.

For too long we waited for someone to rescue us. For a statement to be issued. For a foreign power to pressure. For a new party to be kinder. For history to fix itself. It never happens. Empire never freed its subjects. Fascism never freed its citizens. They only changed the uniform of the jailer and told us to be grateful.

Freedom is not delivered. It is not granted from above with papers and permission. It is not charity. It has to be fought for, claimed, and held by the people who need it. With your voice, with your street, with your refusal to bow. It will be uncomfortable. It will be lonely. It will cost. But that cost is what turns a subject into a citizen. And once you have fought for it yourself and achieved it yourself, no one can ever take it from you and call it a gift again.

text:
On 17 October 1931, Alphonse Capone or more commonly known as Al Capone or Scarface and leader of the Chicago Outfit was convicted of tax evasion. Capone, who had risen to command the criminal organization, became one of America’s most notorious criminals of the 1920’s.

Capone, the son of Italian immigrants and from Brooklyn, New York migrated to Chicago in 1920 to work with crime boss Johnny Torrio. It was also at this time Prohibition, which banned the manufacture, sale, and distribution of alcohol in the United States, took effect. Its supporters believed that doing this would end the effects of alcoholism and addiction. Instead, it resulted in criminal gangs all over the country getting into the business of providing alcohol either by transporting it from other countries or making it themselves and distributing it. Illegal places called speakeasies appeared in cities where people could go for a drink. The vast money made from this allowed these gangs to bribe police, city officials, and judges. It also resulted in fierce competition in some cities like Chicago resulting in vicious gang wars. While these gangs also had their traditional moneymaking via gambling and prostitution, the money made from alcohol was enormous.

When Joe Torrio retired in 1925, Capone assumed control. Capone ran the Chicago Outfit with ruthlessness going to war often other gangs and in particular the North Side Gang led initially by Dion O’Bannion who was killed in 1924 and then Bugs Moran wh0 took over. Violence between these gangs was often public and bloody. It ultimately culminated in the infamous St. Valentine’s Day Massacre of 1929 in which several members of Moran’s gang were slaughtered in a garage. Men presumably with the Capone gang dressed up as cops ordered the men to stand against a wall and shot them dead. It made international headlines resulting in President Hoover directing federal agencies to go after Capone and his supporters.

Capone was a larger-than-life figure that was covered by the press. He lived flamboyantly, wore expensive suits, ate gourmet meals and smoked expensive cigars. He was a businessman, if anyone asked, who gave the people what they wanted. Everyone knew he was the leader of the South Side Gang and that he was enormously wealthy. Pictured in fancy jewelry and often with female companionship, Capone put out a public face that countered those who depicted him otherwise. With all the bribes he paid, he likely thought he was untouchable though he did get 10 months in Holmsberg Prison in Philadelphia for carrying a concealed handgun. It did not slow him down much; he ran his operation from prison.

Bringing him down became a top priority for both the Justice and Treasury Departments. Since they could not rely on any help from Chicago, they created their own task force using a two-pronged approach. The first part was to hit his operations hard using elite units that would target the bootlegging operations. This was led by Eliot Ness who led up this section. Unlike what was shown in both television and movies, this was a large unit that relied on intelligence from friendly newspapers such as the Chicago Daily News. Its publisher, William Strong, had been a strong supporter for getting Hoover to act and provided Ness with information. The raids on the warehouses and other operations took its toll.

The second part, less showy but effective, was to come after him for underreporting his taxable income on his federal tax returns. As this process began to unfold, Capone started getting nervous as they started asking obvious questions as to the sources of his great wealth. He even made an offer to pay for certain years to reduce the sentence and fine. And a letter from his attorney conceding he had underreported told the Treasury agents they were on the right track. With a ledger and his accountant to testify against him, the prosecution was able to lay out a great case of a man living large with access to great sums of money. His spending, covered in the newspapers extensively, came into the trial as well. The jury convicted him of evading $215,000 in taxes with an income of $1,038,654 during a five-year period. Judge Wilkenson gave him the maximum penalty of 11 years, fined him $50,000 and $7,692 in court costs. There was also interest due of $215,000 for the underpayment.

It was the end of Capone’s tenure as head of the Chicago Outfit. He was first sent to the U.S. Penitentiary in Atlanta in May 1932. However Judge Wilkerson received reports special treatment he was receiving, and he would be transferred to Alcatraz in August 1934. In Atlanta, it was found he was suffering from both syphilis and gonorrhea. He also had to be treated for cocaine withdrawal as well. At Alcatraz, he would be in the hospital section due to neurosyphilis that eroded his mental faculties. After his term was up in January 1939, he was sent to another facility to serve out his contempt of court sentence. In November 1939 he would be paroled and sent to the Union Memorial Hospital for treatment.

He ultimately retired to Palm Island Florida and received treatments for neurosyphilis and was able to use the newest drug penicillin which prolonged his life. He died from heart failure on 27 February 1947, at the age of 48. He was originally buried at the Mount Olivet Cemetery in Chicago. His remains were later removed (along with his family’s) to Mount Carmel Cemetery in Hillsdale, Illinois. By the time of his death both his physician and psychiatrist had concluded he had the mentality of a 12-year-old child, a far cry from the days of being flamboyant and ruthless chief of one of the most notorious gangs in the United States.

text:
John Kluge, a former orchestra and music theory teacher at Brownsburg High School in Indiana, has secured a $650,000 settlement from the Brownsburg Community School Corporation after an eight-year legal battle over his refusal, on religious grounds, to use transgender students’ preferred names and pronouns.

Kluge was hired in 2014 and told Principal Bret Daghe on the first day of classes in 2017 that he had a religious objection to the district’s new policy requiring teachers to use the identifiers listed in students’ official records. Officials initially granted him an accommodation allowing him to address every student by last name only, like a sports coach. After complaints from students, teachers and counselors who said the workaround made transgender students feel singled out and hurt, the district withdrew the accommodation in 2018 and told Kluge to comply or resign. He resigned and sued under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, which bars religious discrimination against employees.

The case went through years of appeals before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit ruled in August 2025 that Kluge was entitled to a jury trial, citing the Supreme Court’s 2023 decision in Groff v. DeJoy on religious accommodation. Rather than proceed to trial, the district agreed in March 2026 to pay Kluge $650,000 and to train its senior staff on Title VII’s religious protections. David Cortman, senior counsel at the Alliance Defending Freedom, which represented Kluge, said the settlement “shows teachers that they do not have to bow the knee to ideological mandates that violate their religious beliefs,” adding, “after almost five and a half years, common sense has prevailed at Brownsburg.”

Kluge later wrote in an op-ed for The Indianapolis Star that the payout “won’t bring back the job I love, but it does offer substantial financial compensation... for the loss, hardships and litigation of the last almost seven years.” LGBTQ advocacy groups have criticized the outcome and the Alliance Defending Freedom’s role in the case, while the school district has maintained it does not believe Kluge’s rights were violated.

My ancestors would be pissed off ! FOREWORD
The name Versailles may safely be presumed to have become a family name from the city which is now the seat of the prefect of the departement of Yvelines, Paris Region, in north-central France. The present city of Versailles owes its existence to the famed palace built for Louis XIV between 1601 and 1708 which later became world renowned as the locale at which Germany sued for peace in 1919, ending World War I.
At a reunion of the Versailles-Versaw Family Association (tormerly Tribe of Francis) at Divide Colorado in August 1971 it was suggested and accordingly voted to publish a book of genealogical records of the Versailles-Versaw family.
These are descendants of Julien Vacherot who was born in Versailles, France around 1725 and sent as a soldier to Canada by France between 1744 and
1748. On shipboard nicknames or aliases were given to many of the military men which in future generations often replaced surnames. Julien was hereafter called Julien Vacherot-dit-Versailles.
Family tradition has it that a grandson of Julien fathered twelve sons of which at least six were to settle in the United States. First to come was Francis who left the Province of Quebec at an early age and lived with Indians in New York State for a few years. He then went to Green Bay, Wisconsin and about 1835 became a pioneer settler of the St. Joseph-Benton Harbor area of southwest Michigan. Other brothers followed at different times, part of a great migration from the Montreal area southward. Luke, Levi, Peter and Maxwell joined Francis in Michigan. Benoit, also known as Robert, went first to Dannemora, N.Y. for a few years, and finally joined relatives in Massachusetts
There are several traditions as to how the name Versailles evolved into Ver-saw. The one told by Francis E. Versaw to his daughter Alma and by her to Francis great-grandson: Francis first associates in the United States, probably the Indians, could not correctly pronounce Versailles, which in their dialect came out as Versaw. Versaw was adopted and uniformly used in all Michigan records. We believe that every Versaw we have found belongs to this family and many of the Versailles although three other surnames were given the same "dit Versailles." Most early Massachusetts records list Kobert as Versaille, then followed a period of Versaw. Only in the last half century have Benoit's descendants consistently used Versailles.
In July 1954 Harvey and Elizabeth Versailles began to research the early generations of his ancestors in Quebec. In April 1971 and in August 1971 more parishes were searched in hopes of tinding the baptismal record of Francis. In January 1972 copies of marriages in Montreal in the 19th century were received which completed our records of relatives in Canada.
Elizabeth Versailles, certified as a genealogist in 1966, was glad to offer her services as editor of her husband's family history. We especially appreciate the help of the many priests who served small parishes in Quebec and kept careful records of the baptisms and marriages performed by them, especially those who served St. Constant, St. Philippe, St. Edouard and St. Michel Archanges (Ref. St. Constant et St. Philippe de LaPrairie, 1744-1946, Jean Jacques Le-Febvre) which is where our earliest three or four generations lived for about a century.
Willie King Versaw
Franklin, Nebraska-1971

Copart completes $1.9B acquisition of ACV Auctions.

Copart finalized its acquisition of ACV Auctions on October 16 after its tender offer expired, with approximately 68.43% of ACV’s outstanding shares validly tendered and not withdrawn.

The deal, originally announced in September, valued ACV at $10.50 per share in cash, representing an implied equity value of approximately $1.9 billion and a roughly 45% premium to ACV’s unaffected closing price on August 10.

The merger was completed under Section 251(h) of Delaware law without a stockholder meeting, with ACV surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Copart.

The acquisition expands Copart’s position across the vehicle remarketing ecosystem, pairing its salvage auction dominance with ACV’s digital wholesale marketplace.‌￼

1 And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.

2 (And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.)

3 And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city.

4 And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)

5 To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.

6 And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered.

7 And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

8 And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.

9 And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.

10 And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.

11 For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.

12 And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.

13 And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,

14 Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

15 And it came to pass, as the angels were gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us.

16 And they came with haste, and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.

17 And when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying which was told them concerning this child.

18 And all they that heard it wondered at those things which were told them by the shepherds.

19 But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.

20 And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.

21 And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

22 And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord;

23 (As it is written in the law of the LORD, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;)

24 And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.

25 And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him.

26 And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ.

27 And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,

28 Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said,

29 Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:

30 For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,

31 Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people;

35 (Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.

text:
THE WORSHIP GOD IS SEEKING
When the Heart Meets the Father in Spirit and Truth
John 4:21–24 | NIV
A DIVINE ENCOUNTER THAT CHANGED EVERYTHING
Beside an ancient well in Samaria, Jesus revealed one of Scripture's most extraordinary truths: God is not merely seeking religious activity. He is seeking people who will worship Him in spirit and truth.
This revelation came not inside Jerusalem's magnificent temple, nor before celebrated religious leaders, but during a conversation with a Samaritan woman whose life carried deep personal wounds.
Jesus was about to reveal that true worship transcends geography, religious rivalry, and outward appearances. It begins with a heart awakened to God.
1. THE WOMAN AT THE WELL: GRACE CROSSES BOUNDARIES
John 4:1–20 describes Jesus traveling through Samaria and resting beside Jacob's well near Sychar.
Jews and Samaritans had longstanding religious disagreements. Samaritans worshiped on Mount Gerizim, while Jews recognized Jerusalem as the proper location for temple worship.
When Jesus requested water, the woman was surprised. Jewish men did not ordinarily initiate such conversations with Samaritan women.
Yet Jesus saw beyond social barriers. He spoke of living water, exposed painful realities in her personal life, and offered something infinitely greater than physical satisfaction.
His approach revealed divine compassion without compromising truth.
Before teaching her about worship, Jesus showed her the gracious heart of the One worthy of worship.
2. WORSHIP IS NO LONGER BOUND TO A MOUNTAIN
Jesus declared:
“a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.” — John 4:21
This was revolutionary.
Jesus was not claiming that every religious belief was equally true. He affirmed that salvation comes from the Jews (John 4:22), acknowledging God's covenant revelation through Israel.
Yet He announced a new era in redemptive history.
Through His coming death and resurrection, access to the Father would no longer center on one earthly sanctuary.
God's presence would be known through Jesus Christ and the indwelling Holy Spirit.
Worship would become the privilege of believers everywhere.
3. WHAT DOES WORSHIPING IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH MEAN?
Jesus declared:
“God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.” — John 4:24
Worship in spirit involves sincere inward devotion rather than empty religious performance. In the wider New Testament, genuine worship is made possible through the Holy Spirit, who gives spiritual life and glorifies Christ (John 3:5–8; 16:14).
Worship in truth means responding faithfully to God's revelation, supremely revealed in Jesus Christ.
Jesus proclaimed, “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6).
These dimensions belong together.
Spiritual enthusiasm without biblical truth can become deception. Correct religious knowledge without heartfelt devotion can become lifeless formality.
True worship unites a transformed heart with faithfulness to God's Word.
4. THE FATHER IS ACTIVELY SEEKING WORSHIPERS
Perhaps the passage's most astonishing statement appears in John 4:23:
“they are the kind of worshipers the Father seeks.”
Notice the initiative belongs to God.
Before sinners seek Him, His grace reaches toward them.
The woman arrived seeking ordinary water. She encountered the Messiah offering eternal life.
Jesus soon revealed His identity to her (John 4:26). She left her water jar, returned to her town, and testified about Him.
Many Samaritans subsequently believed (John 4:39–42).
One unexpected conversation became the doorway through which an entire community heard about the Savior.
5. WORSHIP THAT TRANSFORMS EVERYDAY LIFE
Romans 12:1 describes offering our bodies to God as true and proper worship.
Worship therefore extends beyond singing, church gatherings, and spoken prayers.
It includes forgiving those who wound us, resisting temptation, loving difficult neighbors, serving the vulnerable, pursuing holiness, and obeying Christ when nobody is watching.
Jesus taught that love and obedience belong together (John 14:15).
The Holy Trinity is beautifully revealed in this life of worship: the Father receives our devotion, the Son provides our access, and the Holy Spirit strengthens and guides believers (Ephesians 2:18).
Such worship reflects God's Kingdom through righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit (Romans 14:17).
THE HEART OF TRUE WORSHIP
God is not impressed by religious appearances that conceal pride, bitterness, or unbelief.
Jesus taught that some honor God with their lips while their hearts remain far from Him (Matthew 15:8).
The Father seeks more than impressive words. He desires genuine faith, humility, repentance, love, and surrendered hearts.
The Samaritan woman's story reminds us that no troubled past, cultural division, or social rejection places a repentant person beyond Christ's invitation.
True worship is not about finding the perfect place to encounter God.
It is about coming to the Father through Jesus Christ, in the power of the Holy Spirit, with a heart surrendered to His truth.
QUESTIONS FOR REFLECTION
Am I worshiping God from my heart or merely following religious habits?
Does my daily conduct reflect the truth I profess to believe?
What part of my life needs deeper surrender to the Holy Spirit?
CLOSING PRAYER
Heavenly Father, thank You for seeking us in Your extraordinary love. Lord Jesus, cleanse our hearts and draw us into Your truth. Holy Spirit, awaken sincere devotion within us. Remove pride, hypocrisy, and every distraction that competes for our affection. Teach us to worship through humility, obedience, holiness, and love. May our entire lives become a beautiful offering that glorifies the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. In Jesus' mighty name, Amen.

text:
Responsorial Psalm
Psalm 96:1, 3, 4-5, 7-8, 9-10
R. (7b) Give the Lord glory and honor.
Sing to the LORD a new song;
sing to the LORD, all you lands.
Tell his glory among the nations;
among all peoples, his wondrous deeds.
R. Give the Lord glory and honor.
For great is the LORD and highly to be praised;
awesome is he, beyond all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are things of nought,
but the LORD made the heavens.
R. Give the Lord glory and honor.
Give to the LORD, you families of nations,
give to the LORD glory and praise;
give to the LORD the glory due his name!
Bring gifts, and enter his courts.
R. Give the Lord glory and honor.
Worship the LORD, in holy attire;
tremble before him, all the earth;
say among the nations: The LORD is king,
he governs the peoples with equity.
R. Give the Lord glory and honor.
Background: This psalm was sung when David brought the Ark of the Covenant into Jerusalem after God had given Israel victory over the Philistines. It calls every nation to praise the Lord who made the heavens, who is King, and who governs with equity. All false gods are nothing; only the Lord is worthy of glory and honor.
Lesson: We praise God because He first loved us and gave His Son so that we might have eternal life (Jn 3:16). True praise includes turning away from sin and living for Him. Repentance comes before the full joy of salvation: “The interior penance of the Christian can be expressed in many and various ways. Scripture and the Fathers insist above all on three forms, fasting, prayer, and almsgiving, which express conversion in relation to oneself, to God, and to others” (CCC 1434). When we help the poor or serve others out of love, we thank God and open our hearts to the grace He freely offers to the repentant.

11 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying,

12 If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the priests answered and said, No.

text:
Actually, I don't ignore it. Jonah is describing his death and in detail. 

This isn't a controversial opinion. Here is what Dr. Arnold Fruchtenbaum states:
"Verse 6a describes Jonah’s death: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains. This language depicts the prophet’s body sinking to the ocean floor. Thus, Jonah died by drowning, and the earth with its bars closed upon him forever. Job 38: 17; Psalm 9: 13; 107: 18; and Isaiah 38: 10 also refer to these bars (though expressed with different Hebrew terms in some passages), describing them as gates of death. At this point, Jonah’s spirit was separated from his body. His soul entered Sheol, while his physical remains were swallowed by the fish and thereby preserved. Verse 6b introduces Jonah’s resurrection: Yet have you brought up my life from the pit, O YHWH my God. The Hebrew term for “pit,” shachath, is the most common synonym for Sheol in the Hebrew Bible. It appears in passages such as Job 17: 14; 33: 18; Psalm 16: 10; 30: 9; Isaiah 38: 17; and Ezekiel 28: 8. “Bringing up life from the pit” is a phrase often associated with resurrection. This same concept is used of the Messiah in Psalm 16: 10: For you will not leave my soul to Sheol; Neither will you suffer your holy one to see corruption [shachath]. The terminology applied to Messiah’s resurrection in Psalm 16 is likewise used of Jonah in verse 6b. There is no textual reason not to interpret it in the same way— as a resurrection from the dead. The fish, therefore, picked up Jonah’s lifeless body. The prophet’s soul was in Sheol. From there, Jonah prayed for a second opportunity, and God granted it. The resurrection occurred while Jonah’s body was still inside the fish. In verse 7, Jonah further explained the circumstances of his res- urrection and the reason why it occurred: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered YHWH; And my prayer came in unto you, into your holy temple. As previously noted, the phrase “my soul fainted within me” does not refer to a mere fainting spell but to physical death. After reaching Sheol, Jonah prayed the second prayer. The assertion that this prayer came into YHWH’s holy temple confirms that God received Jonah’s plea. As a result, the prophet was resurrected. Taken literally, Jonah 2 thus far presents a coherent sequence of events that highlights Jonah’s descent, death, and restoration to life. First, Jonah was thrown overboard and was still on the surface of the water, bobbing amid the waves. At that point, he offered his first prayer (v. 4)— a prayer of recognition that it was God who had placed him in this dire situation. Eventually, Jonah sank beneath the surface and drowned, and his body descended to the bottoms of the mountains in the sea, while his soul entered Sheol. There, from the realm of the dead, he prayed his second prayer (v. 7, also mentioned retrospectively in verse 2). The purpose of this prayer was to ask for a second chance to fulfill his divine commission. This second prayer was offered after Jonah had been dead for three days. God responded to this plea by raising Jonah from the dead. The resurrection occurred while the prophet’s body was still within the fish’s abdomen. Following this miraculous restoration to life, Jonah offered his third and final prayer (v. 2). In this prayer, he reflected on the entire sequence of events, including references to both the first and second prayers. Ultimately, Jonah was delivered from the fish."

Arnold G. Fruchtenbaum. OT - Minor Prophets Vol 2 Obediah, Jonah, Micah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah (Kindle Locations 1854-1860). Kindle Edition. "

The Minneapolis Third Precinct burned on May 28, 2020, while Donald Trump was president. That's a fact.

But claiming Trump "did nothing" is historically inaccurate.

Minnesota Governor Tim Walz activated the National Guard before the precinct burned. Trump publicly condemned the violence, offered federal assistance, and later threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act.

State and local officials had primary responsibility for maintaining order, but that doesn't automatically absolve the federal government of accountability.

Here's the real issue: Why were authorities unable to prevent the destruction despite warnings and escalating violence?

We cannot demand federal intervention in one situation while condemning it in another simply because the political parties have changed.

The standard must remain the same regardless of who occupies the White House. Public safety, constitutional authority, and government accountability should never be partisan.

text:
Today, a small moment reminded me of one of the greatest lessons from my pilgrimage to Sinai.

Our Orthodox mission leases part of a local Anglican church, and sometimes first-time visitors unknowingly park in the spaces reserved for the Anglicans, which causes friction.

Today, when that happened, I stepped outside carrying a candle I had received from the ossuary at Sinai. I had lit one and was holding the other to give to Father.

Instead of letting the moment become another disagreement, I offered the Anglicans the second candle as a gift, explaining that I was bringing them a little light from Sinai. I had received these candles after praying for peace, our troops and for Texas.

They wanted to hear about my pilgrimage, what I had learned, and how we use our candles. I told them what may have been the greatest lesson of all:

We seem to have lost the ability to extend grace without first demanding that someone think exactly as we do.

They agreed.

We talked about the similarities in how we use our candles, and by the end of the conversation, they were even talking about possibly joining me on a future pilgrimage.

Sometimes, the door to understanding doesn't open through a debate, a correction, or a demand that someone follow our rules. 

Sometimes, it opens when we offer a little light instead.

I went to Sinai praying for peace. Today, I was reminded that peace begins in the small moments, right where we are.

Lord, have mercy. 🕯️

text:
🧪 A post claims a 71-year-old Texas man with glioblastoma had “clear scans” after six months taking ivermectin, mebendazole, and CBD.

A story like this can offer hope, but the screenshot does not provide the medical records needed to evaluate it. We do not see the original pathology, the full MRI history, what other cancer treatments he received, or how long the reported response lasted. “Clear scans” is not enough on its own to establish a cure or identify what caused the change.

Ivermectin has not undergone the rigorous human trials needed to show that it is safe and effective as a cancer treatment. Mebendazole has been studied in glioma research, but that does not validate this three-drug protocol or prove it works for glioblastoma.

The claim that someone has “helped over 9,000 patients” also needs transparent, independently reviewed outcome data. Testimonials cannot tell patients how often a treatment works, what risks it carries, or whether it is better than established care.

Glioblastoma is a serious diagnosis. Treatment decisions should be based on a patient’s tumor details, oncology team, and credible clinical evidence. Promising ideas deserve well-designed trials, not unsupported promises.

⚕️ Follow @mcgill_medicine for evidence-focused cancer research.

text:
🚨 AMERICANS ARE GETTING RIPPED OFF BY RESTAURANT TIP SCREENS — AND THIS CUSTOMER JUST CAUGHT ONE ON CAMERA

A customer at Texas Roadhouse noticed something seriously wrong with the suggested tip on his bill.

His total was $66. 
The screen suggested $16 for a 20% tip.

There's just one problem.

20% of $66 is $13.20.

That's an extra $2.80 the customer was being prompted to leave.

Now imagine how many people hit that button without ever checking the math.

And it gets worse.

Another customer left his waitress a massive $300 tip, only for her to return with a handwritten note asking him to pay in cash instead.

She even offered to reprint the receipt so he could remove the card tip entirely.

Now customers are questioning whether their electronic tips are actually reaching the employees who earned them.

Restaurants are already charging Americans an arm and a leg for food, then shoving tip screens in their faces like customers owe them another paycheck.

And apparently, now customers have to double check the math themselves.

Why are Americans expected to blindly hand over 20% tips when restaurants can't even make their suggested amounts add up?
